scenario: 百万用户的聊天应用分散在几十台服务器上，每条消息都要先知道收件人连在哪台。
scenario_en: A chat app with millions of users spread across dozens of servers has to work out which server the recipient sits on before every single message.
q: 聊天应用用「一张数据库表存 用户→服务器 映射」来做消息路由，会引入什么问题？
q_en: What problem appears if a chat app stores user-to-server routing in one database table?
options: 只要给这张映射表建好索引，再配上合适的读写分离，查询性能瓶颈自然就不存在了
数据库变成单点故障，还给每条消息多一次查库延迟，规模一大查询就把库打爆成瓶颈
换成主从读写分离部署之后，这个方案就完全没有隐患了
这套方案完全没有任何问题，可以直接原样上线到生产环境
options_en: Just add an index to that mapping table, throw in some read/write splitting, and the query bottleneck simply goes away.
The database becomes a single point of failure, adds a lookup to every message, and gets hammered into a bottleneck at scale.
Switch to a primary-replica read/write split and the design has no more issues at all.
There is no problem at all — ship this as-is straight to production.
why: 库挂了整个聊天系统瘫痪；每条消息先查库再路由；百万用户级别的查询压力巨大——协调问题不是「加张表」能优雅解决的。
why_en: A database mapping becomes a single point of failure, adds a lookup to every message, and turns into a bottleneck at scale.
optionExplanations: 索引能缓解查询变慢，但解决不了单点故障和每条消息一次查库的延迟问题，规模一大照样被打爆。
对：数据库既是单点故障又给每条消息叠加一次查库延迟，用户量上去后数据库自己先顶不住。
读写分离能分摊读压力，但主库仍是唯一写入点，故障和路由延迟这两个根本问题都还在。
这套方案完全没有问题的说法回避了单点故障和每条消息一次查库延迟的事实，不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Indexing helps query speed but does not remove the single point of failure or the extra per-message database lookup — the DB still gets crushed at scale.
Right: the database is both a single point of failure and an added lookup per message, so it gets overwhelmed once user count climbs.
Read/write splitting spreads reads, but the primary is still the one write path, so the SPOF and per-message latency remain.
Claiming there is no problem ignores the single point of failure and the extra per-message lookup — it does not hold up.

scenario: 聊天应用给「用户→服务器」路由表挂了缓存，但用户随时断线重连、被调度到别的服务器。
scenario_en: A chat app puts a cache in front of its user-to-server routing table, but users reconnect at any moment and get moved to a different server.
q: 给「用户→服务器」的数据库加缓存来提速，新问题是什么？
q_en: What new problem appears if you cache the user-to-server mapping table?
options: 缓存服务器需要额外的机器采购、长期运维投入和团队人力成本，预算和排期都完全扛不住这笔额外开销
用户到服务器的映射表数据体量太大，普通的内存型缓存根本存不下这么多条目
缓存一致性问题：用户换到别的服务器后，原服务器的缓存仍指向旧地址，消息因此发丢
引入缓存之后，每一次写库操作都必须先等待缓存完成同步才能返回给调用方
options_en: Cache servers need extra machine purchases, ongoing ops investment, and team headcount — the budget and timeline cannot absorb this extra cost.
The user-to-server mapping is far too large for an ordinary in-memory cache to hold.
Cache consistency: once a user moves to a different server, the old server's cache still points at the stale address, so messages get lost.
After adding a cache, every write must first wait for the cache sync to complete before returning to the caller.
why: 路由信息是会变的：缓存过期或失效不及时就把消息发去旧服务器——这正是「需要变更通知」的根源。
why_en: Caching the mapping creates staleness: a user who reconnects elsewhere leaves other servers routing messages to the old server.
optionExplanations: 缓存机器要花钱是真实成本，但它不是这道题真正要暴露的坑——缓存数据变旧才是。
映射表体积不大，普通内存缓存完全装得下，存不下不是这里的真实限制。
对：用户换了服务器后，其它服务器的缓存还指着旧地址，消息因此发丢，这是缓存必须解决的一致性问题。
缓存架构不要求写请求等缓存同步完成才返回，那样反而失去了缓存加速的意义。
optionExplanations_en: Extra cache machines cost money, but that is not the trap this question is pointing at — staleness is.
The mapping table is not that large — an ordinary in-memory cache holds it fine, so size is not the real limit here.
Right: once a user reconnects elsewhere, other servers' caches still point at the old server, so messages get lost until the cache catches up.
Caches are not designed to make every write wait for cache sync before returning — that would defeat the point of caching.

scenario: 聊天集群有上百台服务器，路由变更靠服务器之间两两直连广播来同步。
scenario_en: The chat cluster runs over a hundred servers and syncs routing changes by having every server broadcast directly to every other one.
q: 改成「服务器之间直接广播变更」呢？规模变大后的问题是？
q_en: If servers broadcast routing changes directly to each other, what breaks at scale?
options: 每台服务器都要和其它所有服务器保持连接，形成 n² 条连接和海量广播流量，扩展性很差
广播出去的每条变更消息都会被强制加密，导致传播延迟明显上升，和扩展性无关
这套方案真正的瓶颈只在每台服务器的磁盘写入吞吐上，跟服务器之间要维护多少条连接毫无关系
服务器间直接广播天生比查一次数据库还慢，所以规模变大反而不是问题
options_en: Every server has to keep a connection to every other server — n-squared connections and a flood of broadcast traffic that does not scale.
Every broadcast change gets force-encrypted, raising latency, but that has nothing to do with scalability.
The real bottleneck of this design is only each server's disk write throughput, nothing to do with how many inter-server connections must be maintained.
Direct server-to-server broadcast is inherently slower than a database query, so scaling up is not actually a problem.
why: 连接数 ≈ 服务器数 × 服务器数（即 n²），不是按频道或用户数算：几十上百台服务器时广播风暴和连接管理都不可维护。
why_en: Connections ≈ server count × server count (n squared), not channel or user count: full-mesh broadcasting floods the network as the cluster grows.
optionExplanations: 对：全互联意味着每台都要连所有其它机器，连接数和广播流量随节点数平方增长，规模一大根本扛不住。
加密确实会加延迟，但那和这里问的可扩展性瓶颈没关系，答非所问。
真正的瓶颈是连接数随节点数平方增长，不是磁盘吞吐——把原因归到磁盘写入是找错了对象。
广播和查库谁快是另一个问题，这里的核心是连接数随节点数平方级增长，规模变大才是灾难。
optionExplanations_en: Right: full mesh means every server connects to every other, so connections and broadcast traffic grow with the square of the cluster size — unmanageable at scale.
Encryption does add latency, but that has nothing to do with the scalability question being asked here.
The real bottleneck is connections growing with the square of node count, not disk throughput — blaming disk writes points at the wrong cause.
Whether broadcast beats a database lookup is a different question; the real issue is connections exploding as n squared.

scenario: 聊天集群自建心跳探活：服务器互相 ping，跨机房链路偶尔会抖动几秒。
scenario_en: The chat cluster rolls its own heartbeat detection — servers ping each other, and the cross-datacenter link occasionally stalls for a few seconds.
q: 自己实现心跳做故障检测，会撞上什么经典难题？
q_en: What classic problem do you hit when you build your own heartbeat-based failure detector?
options: 心跳包发送频率一旦调高，会把内网带宽完全占满，还可能引发级联的网络抖动和丢包，拖慢其它业务流量
频繁的心跳探测请求会把正在休眠省电模式的服务器意外唤醒过来
服务器只要 CPU 短暂过载，就会彻底无法发出任何心跳包
网络分区：Server 2 活着，但与 Server 1 网络不通，节点间对「谁死了」的判断不一致
options_en: Cranking up heartbeat frequency saturates the internal network bandwidth and can trigger cascading jitter and packet loss.
Frequent heartbeat probes accidentally wake servers that are in low-power sleep mode.
A server that is briefly CPU-overloaded becomes completely unable to send any heartbeat.
Network partition: Server 2 is alive but unreachable from Server 1, so nodes disagree about who is dead.
why: 「挂了」和「网络不通」无法区分，不同观察者得出不同结论——这正是需要共识协议的原因。
why_en: Heartbeats hit the network partition problem: a live server can look dead to some peers, leaving the cluster with inconsistent views.

termDefinitions.meaning: 网络分区：集群内部分服务器之间的网络连接中断，但各自仍在运行，导致不同节点看到不一致的存活视图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A network partition is when part of a cluster loses connectivity to another part while both sides keep running, so nodes disagree about who is alive.

optionExplanations: 调高心跳频率确实可能占带宽，但这不是心跳检测最经典也最难绕开的那个坑。
心跳探测唤醒休眠机器是无关的边缘场景，不是自建心跳检测要面对的核心难题。
CPU 短暂过载确实可能让心跳延迟，但不是『判断谁死了』这个难题的根源。
对：Server 2 其实活着，只是和 Server 1 网络不通，不同节点对『谁挂了』得出不同结论，这正是网络分区的经典难题。
optionExplanations_en: Cranking up heartbeat rate can add bandwidth pressure, but that is not the classic hard problem self-built heartbeats run into.
Waking sleeping machines with heartbeats is an unrelated edge case, not the core challenge here.
Brief CPU overload can delay a heartbeat, but that is not the root of the 'who is dead' disagreement.
Right: Server 2 is actually alive, just unreachable from Server 1, so different nodes reach different conclusions about who is dead — the classic partition problem.

scenario: 聊天应用要在几十台服务器间共享路由、互相探活并选出一台做协调，团队不想自己造协议。
scenario_en: A chat app must share routing across dozens of servers, detect failures, and elect one coordinator — and the team does not want to invent its own protocols.
q: ZooKeeper 被设计来解决哪些分布式系统的基本难题？（多选）
q_en: Which distributed-systems problems is ZooKeeper designed to solve? (Select all that apply.)
options: 服务发现与配置共享
故障检测与 leader 选举
分布式共识
海量图片的存储与分发
options_en: Service discovery and shared configuration
Failure detection and leader election
Distributed consensus
Storing and distributing massive photo libraries
why: 服务发现、配置管理、故障检测、leader 选举、共识——这些做对极难（要处理部分失败、网络延迟还要保持一致），ZK 把它们打包解决。
why_en: ZooKeeper packages service discovery, configuration sharing, failure detection, leader election, and consensus so you do not build those algorithms yourself.

termDefinitions.meaning: leader 选举：在一组节点里选出一个节点专门负责协调关键操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Leader election is choosing one node in a group to coordinate critical operations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式共识：多台机器在网络延迟和部分故障下，就同一个状态达成一致的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Distributed consensus is the process by which multiple machines agree on one state despite network delay and partial failures.

optionExplanations: 服务发现与配置共享是 ZK 的招牌用途之一：让所有节点看到同一份最新配置和拓扑。
故障检测与 leader 选举是 ZK 要解决的核心协调难题，靠临时节点和顺序节点实现。
分布式共识是 ZK 存在的根本原因——多机在延迟和部分故障下也要认同同一个状态。
海量图片存储与分发是对象存储的活，ZNode 设计上限只有约 1MB，装不下也不是它的定位。
optionExplanations_en: Service discovery and shared config is one of ZooKeeper's headline uses: every node sees the same current topology.
Failure detection and leader election are core coordination problems ZooKeeper solves with ephemeral and sequential nodes.
Distributed consensus is the whole reason ZooKeeper exists — machines agreeing on one state despite delay and partial failure.
Storing and distributing massive photo libraries is an object-store job; znodes cap out around a megabyte, so this is not what ZooKeeper is for.

scenario: 聊天集群的每台服务器都要读到同一份最新的路由与配置视图，才能把消息发对地方。
scenario_en: Every server in the chat cluster needs the same up-to-date view of routing and config, otherwise messages go to the wrong place.
q: 理解 ZooKeeper 最好的心智模型是？
q_en: What is the best mental model for ZooKeeper?
options: 一套专门做任务异步分发和排队的消息队列系统
一个「同步的元数据文件系统」：每个接入节点看到的都是同一份一致数据视图
一个专门存海量图片、视频等二进制大文件的对象存储服务，走的是完全不同的定位
一个支持复杂 SQL 联表查询的传统关系型数据库
options_en: A message queue for asynchronous task dispatch and buffering.
A synchronized metadata filesystem where every connected node sees the same consistent view.
An object store for massive binary files like images and video, serving a completely different purpose.
A traditional relational database with complex SQL joins.
why: ZK 像一棵所有参与者共享、保持一致的元数据树——这份跨服务器的一致视图正是它做协调的能力来源。
why_en: Think of ZooKeeper as a synchronized metadata filesystem where every connected node shares the same consistent view.
optionExplanations: 消息队列擅长异步分发和缓冲任务，但 ZK 给的是一份所有节点共享的一致视图，不是排队转发。
对：把它想成一个所有连接节点看到同一份数据的『同步元数据文件系统』，这份一致视图正是协调能力的来源。
对象存储专为海量二进制大文件设计，ZNode 只放小量协调数据，定位完全不同。
关系型数据库支持复杂联表查询，ZK 没有查询语言，也不是拿来做事务查询的。
optionExplanations_en: A message queue is built for async dispatch and buffering, not for giving every node the same consistent view — that is ZooKeeper's job.
Right: think of it as a synchronized metadata filesystem where every connected node sees the same consistent view — that shared view is where its coordination power comes from.
Object stores are built for massive binary files; znodes only hold small coordination data, a completely different role.
A relational database supports complex joins and a query language — ZooKeeper has neither and is not meant for transactional queries.

scenario: 要把聊天应用的路由映射和配置放进 ZK：数千个用户条目，还有人想顺手存用户头像图片。
scenario_en: You are moving chat routing and config into ZooKeeper — thousands of user entries — and someone suggests parking user avatar images there too.
q: 关于 ZNode 的数据特征，正确的是？
q_en: Which statement about ZNode data is correct?
options: ZNode 是专门用来存放大体积文件的，因此节点数量通常很少，也不适合存协调数据
ZNode 的取值类型受限，只能存放整数或浮点数这类数字
ZNode 只存小量协调数据（通常 <1MB），节点数量可到数千量级；不放图片、大文档
ZNode 组织成完全扁平的命名空间，任何一个节点都不能再挂载子节点，因此无法表达路径层级关系
options_en: ZNodes are meant for storing large files, so there are usually only a few of them, and they are not fit for coordination data.
ZNode values are restricted to numeric types like integers or floats.
ZNodes hold small coordination data, typically under one megabyte, with counts up to the thousands — not images or large documents.
ZNodes form a completely flat namespace where no node can mount child nodes, so path hierarchy cannot be expressed.
why: ZNode 按路径组织成树（如 /app1/config），既能有子节点又能存数据+元数据；定位是协调元数据，不是大块数据。
why_en: ZNodes hold small coordination data under one megabyte each, organized in a large hierarchical tree, not bulk data.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZNode：ZooKeeper 树形命名空间里的一个数据节点，既能存少量数据也能有子节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A znode is a node in ZooKeeper's hierarchical namespace that can hold a small amount of data and also have child nodes.

optionExplanations: ZNode 恰恰不是拿来存大文件的，它的设计上限只有约 1MB，节点数量反而可以到几千个。
ZNode 能存任意字节数据（通常是字符串/JSON），不限制成数字类型。
对：ZNode 只放小于 1MB 的协调数据，数量可到几千个，不放图片或大文档。
ZNode 恰恰是层级结构，一个节点下面完全可以挂子节点，并不是扁平的、不能有子节点。
optionExplanations_en: ZNodes are the opposite of a large-file store — the guideline caps them around one megabyte, while node counts can reach the thousands.
A znode can hold arbitrary byte data, typically strings or JSON — it is not restricted to numeric types.
Right: znodes hold small coordination data under a megabyte, with counts reaching the thousands, not images or big documents.
ZNodes are in fact hierarchical: a node can hold children below it, so it is not flat and childless.

q: 补全三种 ZNode 类型：
q_en: Fill in the three ZNode types.
text: {{Persistent}}（持久）节点：显式删除前一直存在；{{Ephemeral}}（临时）节点：创建它的会话结束（断连或超时）就自动删除；{{Sequential}}（顺序）节点：名字自动追加单调递增计数器。
why: 三种节点是所有 ZK 配方的原料：配置用持久、活性跟踪用临时、排序/锁/选举用顺序（常与临时组合）。
why_en: Persistent nodes live until deleted, ephemeral nodes vanish when their session ends, and sequential nodes get an auto-incrementing counter in their name.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持久节点：显式删除前会一直存在，不受客户端会话影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A persistent znode stays until explicitly deleted, regardless of client sessions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 临时节点：创建它的客户端会话一结束（断连或超时）就自动被删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ephemeral znode is automatically deleted when the client session that created it ends.

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序节点：ZooKeeper 自动在节点名后追加单调递增的计数器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequential znode gets a monotonically increasing counter automatically appended to its name by ZooKeeper.

scenario: 要在 ZK 里存聊天应用的配置：最大消息长度、限速参数——改了才变，不随会话消失。
scenario_en: You need to store chat-app configuration in ZooKeeper, such as max message size and rate limits. It changes only when edited and must not disappear with a client session.
q: 该用哪种 ZNode？
q_en: Which ZNode type should you use?
options: Ephemeral（临时）节点——但它会随客户端会话结束而消失
Sequential ephemeral（顺序临时）节点——既顺序编号又跟会话绑定
不用 ZNode，把配置塞进外部消息队列里发布
Persistent（持久）节点——不随会话变化，显式删除前一直存在
options_en: Ephemeral — but it disappears the moment the client session ends.
Sequential ephemeral — numbered in order and still tied to a session.
Skip znodes entirely and push the config through an external message queue.
Persistent — stays until explicitly deleted, unaffected by session changes.
why: 配置数据要求「直到显式删除/修改前一直存在」，持久节点正合适；临时节点会随会话断开而消失。
why_en: Configuration like max message size belongs in persistent nodes that survive until explicitly changed.
whenOtherWins: 跟踪「谁活着」（服务器/用户在线状态）时要用临时节点，让崩溃自动清理。
tradeoff: 持久节点「一直存在」的可靠配置 vs 临时节点「随会话消失」的活性跟踪
codeSample:
# 存最大消息长度等配置（默认就是 Persistent）
create /chat-app/config/max_message_size "1024"
create /chat-app/config/rate_limit "100/sec"
# 不带 -e / -s 标志
optionExplanations: 临时节点会在服务器重启会话时被清空，配置这种要求『改了才变』的数据经不起这种消失。
顺序编号对纯配置毫无意义，而且仍然绑定会话，会话一断配置照样消失。
消息队列是流式管道，读不到『当前值是多少』，查配置需要能随时读到最新状态的存储，不是队列。
对：持久节点在显式删除或修改前一直存在，不受会话影响，正好匹配『改了才变、不随会话消失』的配置需求。
optionExplanations_en: Ephemeral nodes get wiped whenever a server's session restarts, and config that should only change on edit cannot survive that.
Ordering adds nothing for plain config, and it is still session-bound, so the value still disappears when the session ends.
A queue is a stream, not queryable storage — you cannot ask it 'what is the current value', which config reads need.
Right: persistent nodes survive until explicitly deleted or changed, unaffected by sessions, exactly matching config that only changes when edited.

scenario: 每台聊天服务器启动时在 ZK 注册自己（IP:端口），要求服务器崩溃后注册信息自动消失，别人能据此发现故障。
scenario_en: Each chat server registers its IP and port in ZooKeeper on startup. If the server crashes, that registration must disappear automatically so other servers can detect the failure.
q: 该用哪种 ZNode？
q_en: Which ZNode type should you use?
options: Ephemeral（临时）节点——服务器的会话一结束就自动被删除
Persistent（持久）节点——注册信息会一直留着，除非手动清理
只加 Sequential 顺序编号，不用临时特性
用操作系统里的普通文件记录服务器状态
options_en: Ephemeral — the registration is deleted automatically the moment the server's session ends.
Persistent — the registration stays around until someone manually cleans it up.
Just add sequential numbering and skip the ephemeral property.
Track server state in a plain OS-level file.
why: 临时节点与会话绑定：服务器崩溃 → 会话超时 → 节点自动消失 → watcher 收到通知。这是 ZK 故障检测的核心机制。
why_en: Ephemeral nodes disappear automatically when the creator's session ends, which is exactly how ZooKeeper detects dead servers.
whenOtherWins: 存配置这类「不该随会话消失」的数据必须用持久节点。
tradeoff: 会话绑定的自动清理（临时）vs 需要手动维护的长期记录（持久）

termDefinitions.meaning: 临时节点：与创建者的客户端会话绑定，会话结束就被自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ephemeral znode is bound to its creator's session and is deleted automatically when that session ends.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持久节点：不跟随会话变化，需要显式删除或修改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A persistent znode is unaffected by sessions and requires an explicit delete or update.

optionExplanations: 对：临时节点绑定服务器的会话，崩溃后会话超时，注册信息自动消失，其它服务器立刻能感知故障。
持久节点要手动清理，服务器崩溃后注册信息会一直留着，误导其它服务器以为它还活着。
顺序编号不解决『崩溃后要自动消失』这个需求，少了临时特性照样留着死服务器的痕迹。
本地文件只在这台机器上可见，其它服务器读不到，也没法在崩溃时被集群统一感知。
optionExplanations_en: Right: ephemeral nodes are tied to the server's session, so a crash times out the session and the registration disappears automatically, letting others detect the failure.
Persistent nodes need manual cleanup, so a crashed server's registration lingers and misleads others into thinking it is still alive.
Sequential numbering alone does not make the entry vanish on crash — without the ephemeral property, the dead server's trace stays.
A local OS file is only visible on that one machine — other servers cannot read it or be notified when it crashes.

scenario: 需要给一组并发创建的节点排出全局顺序（比如消息排序、锁队列、选举排队）。
scenario_en: You need a global order for nodes created concurrently, such as message ordering, a lock queue, or an election queue.
q: 该用哪种 ZNode 特性？
q_en: Which ZNode feature should you use?
options: Persistent（持久）节点——数据一直存在，但不提供任何排序能力
Sequential（顺序）节点——ZooKeeper 自动在名字后追加单调递增的计数器
自己生成随机 UUID 拼进节点名，指望它天然有序，省去服务端排序的麻烦，实现起来也更简单
用客户端本地系统时间戳给节点命名排序
options_en: Persistent — the data stays forever but provides no ordering at all.
Sequential — ZooKeeper automatically appends a monotonically increasing counter to the name.
Generate a random UUID yourself and hope it happens to sort in order, skipping server-side ordering work.
Name nodes using each client's local system timestamp.
why: 顺序节点由 ZK 统一分配递增编号（msg-0000000001…），天然形成全局顺序——锁与选举配方都建立在它上面。
why_en: Sequential nodes get a monotonically increasing counter appended by ZooKeeper, giving a global order for locks and elections.
whenOtherWins: 客户端本地时间戳会因时钟漂移乱序，不能用来定全局顺序。
tradeoff: 服务端统一分配的单调序号（Sequential）vs 客户端自算的标识（UUID/时间戳）不保证全局顺序
codeSample:
# 顺序节点：ZooKeeper 自动追加计数器
create -s /chat-app/channels/global/msg- "Alice: Hello everyone!"
# 实际路径 -> /chat-app/channels/global/msg-0000000001

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序节点：ZooKeeper 在创建时自动追加单调递增计数器后缀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequential znode automatically gets a monotonically increasing counter suffix from ZooKeeper at creation time.

termDefinitions.meaning: UUID（通用唯一识别码）：一种几乎不会重复但没有顺序含义的随机标识符。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A UUID is a nearly-unique random identifier that carries no ordering information.

optionExplanations: 持久节点确实一直存在，但完全没有排序能力，解决不了『谁先谁后』的问题。
对：顺序节点由 ZooKeeper 统一分配单调递增的编号，天然给出全局顺序，锁和选举都建立在它上面。
随机 UUID 不带任何顺序信息，两个客户端谁先创建根本看不出来。
客户端本地时钟会漂移，不同机器算出的时间戳顺序不可靠，不能当全局顺序用。
optionExplanations_en: Persistent nodes do persist, but they provide no ordering at all, so they cannot answer 'who came first'.
Right: sequential nodes get a monotonically increasing counter assigned centrally by ZooKeeper, giving a natural global order that locks and elections build on.
A random UUID carries no ordering information — you cannot tell which client created its node first.
Client clocks drift, so timestamps from different machines do not give a reliable global order.

scenario: Server 2 启动时要在 /chat-app/servers/ 下注册自己，且崩溃后注册自动清除。
scenario_en: Server 2 needs to register itself under /chat-app/servers/, and the registration must be removed automatically if it crashes.
q: 正确的命令是？
q_en: Which ZooKeeper command is correct?
options: create /chat-app/servers/server2 "192.168.1.102:8080"
create -s /chat-app/servers/server2 "192.168.1.102:8080"
create -e /chat-app/servers/server2 "192.168.1.102:8080"
set /chat-app/servers/server2 "192.168.1.102:8080"
options_en: Run create with no flag — a persistent node at that path.
Run create with -s — a persistent node with an auto-appended sequence number.
Run create with -e — an ephemeral node tied to this session.
Run set — update the value of an existing node instead of creating one.
why: -e 创建临时节点：Server 2 崩溃后它注册的节点（含它名下用户的节点）自动消失，其他服务器经 watch 得到通知。
why_en: The -e flag creates an ephemeral node that vanishes automatically if server two crashes.
whenOtherWins: 不带 -e 的普通 create 用于持久配置；-s 用于需要顺序编号的场景。
tradeoff: 带 -e 的临时节点（会话绑定、崩溃自动清理）vs 不带标志的持久节点（需要手动清理）
codeSample:
# 服务器注册（临时节点）
create -e /chat-app/servers/server2 "192.168.1.102:8080"

# Bob 连接到 Server 2 时：
create -e /chat-app/users/bob "server2"

# Server 2 崩溃 => 两个节点都自动消失!

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper CLI 创建临时节点的命令，-e 表示 ephemeral，随会话结束删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: create -e is the ZooKeeper CLI command that makes an ephemeral node, tied to the client session.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper CLI 创建顺序节点的命令，-s 表示 sequential，自动加递增计数器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: create -s is the ZooKeeper CLI command that makes a sequential node with an auto-incrementing counter.

optionExplanations: 不带标志的 create 会建一个持久节点，服务器崩溃后这条注册记录不会自动消失。
-s 只加顺序编号，节点仍是持久的，崩溃后注册信息照样留在树上。
对：-e 建的是临时节点，绑定这次会话；Server 2 崩溃后会话超时，这个节点自动删除。
set 是修改已存在节点的值，这里节点还不存在，用 set 会直接报错。
optionExplanations_en: Plain create with no flag makes a persistent node — it will not vanish automatically when the server crashes.
-s only adds sequential numbering; the node is still persistent, so the registration stays after a crash.
Right: -e creates an ephemeral node tied to this session, so when Server 2 crashes and its session times out, the node deletes itself automatically.
set updates an existing node's value — the node does not exist yet here, so set would just fail.

scenario: 聊天应用已接入 ZK，路由写在 /chat-app/users/<name>；Alice 在 Server 1，Bob 在 Server 2。
scenario_en: The chat app now runs on ZooKeeper with routing under /chat-app/users/<name>; Alice is on Server 1 and Bob is on Server 2.
q: 有了 ZK 之后，Server 1 上的 Alice 给 Bob 发消息，路由怎么走？
q_en: With ZooKeeper in place, how does Alice on Server 1 route a message to Bob?
options: 把这条消息广播给集群里全部在线服务器，让目标服务器自己认领处理，省去查表这一步，实现起来也更简单，还完全不用维护用户到服务器的映射
先查询一个独立维护的中心数据库表，从中拿到 Bob 当前所在的服务器地址
依次轮询集群里的每一台服务器，逐个询问『Bob 是不是连在你这台机器上』
Server 1 查 /chat-app/users/bob 得知 Bob 在 Server 2，据此直接路由消息
options_en: Broadcast the message to every online server in the cluster and let the right one claim it, skipping the lookup entirely — simpler to implement, with no user-to-server mapping to maintain.
First query a separately maintained central database table to find Bob's current server address.
Poll every server in the cluster one by one, asking 'is Bob connected to your machine?'
Server 1 looks up /chat-app/users/bob, learns Bob is on Server 2, and routes there directly.
why: 用户→服务器映射本身就是一个 ZNode；Server 1 靠本地缓存+watch 拿到最新值，Bob 换服务器时该节点自动更新，不用每条消息现查。
why_en: Server one looks up Bob's znode to learn he is on server two and routes the message there, with the mapping kept current automatically.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Server 1"] --> B["Local route cache"]
  B --> C["Bob on Server 2"]
  D["ZooKeeper"] -->|"watch update"| B
optionExplanations: 广播给全体服务器让一条消息变成 N 份流量，正是引入 ZK 之前想避免的低效方案，省掉映射的代价是带宽爆炸。
独立维护的中心数据库正是引入 ZK 之前的旧方案，会带来单点故障和每条消息的查库延迟。
逐台轮询问『Bob 在不在你这』延迟随集群规模线性增长，完全不现实。
对：Server 1 直接查 /chat-app/users/bob 这个 ZNode，本地缓存配合 watch 保持最新，不用每条消息现查。
optionExplanations_en: Broadcasting to all servers turns one message into N copies of traffic — exactly the inefficiency ZK was introduced to avoid; skipping the mapping costs a bandwidth explosion.
A separately maintained central database is the old pre-ZooKeeper design, bringing back the single point of failure and per-message lookup latency.
Polling every server one by one to ask 'is Bob here' scales latency linearly with cluster size — not realistic.
Right: Server 1 looks up the /chat-app/users/bob znode directly, with a local cache kept fresh by watches, so it does not query fresh for every message.

scenario: 聊天应用有数百万在线用户。有人提议给每个在线用户建一个 ZNode 来做路由。
scenario_en: The chat app has millions of online users. One proposal is to create one ZNode per online user for routing.
q: 更可扩展的做法是？
q_en: What is the more scalable routing design?
options: 照原计划做，ZooKeeper 的写入能力足够扛住百万级节点，不需要额外设计
只让服务器注册进 ZK，用户按 ID 用一致性哈希映射到服务器，ZK 只跟踪服务器
把全部在线用户列表塞进同一个大 ZNode 里存着
给每个在线用户各建 5 个 ZNode 做多副本冗余备份，靠副本数量来抵御节点故障、防止用户状态丢失
options_en: Go ahead as planned — ZooKeeper's write throughput can handle millions of nodes without any extra design work.
Register only servers in ZooKeeper and map users to servers by consistent hashing on user ID.
Stuff the entire list of online users into one big znode.
Create five znodes per online user as redundant replicas, relying on replica count to survive node failures and avoid losing user state.
why: ZK 的写压力 ≈ 服务器数量，不随用户数增长：跟踪几十台服务器（临时节点，故障秒级发现）+ 哈希函数定位用户，用户量再涨也只是二级成本，量级立刻可控。
why_en: ZooKeeper's write load ≈ server count, not user count: track a few dozen servers with ephemeral nodes for fast failure detection, and hash users to them — user growth is only a secondary cost.
whenOtherWins: 用户量小（几千）时按用户建节点也行，简单直接。
tradeoff: ZK 只跟踪少量服务器节点（可扩展）vs 给每个用户建节点（写路径压垮 + 内存爆）

termDefinitions.meaning: 一致性哈希：把 key 和节点都映射到一个哈希环上，节点增减时只影响环上邻近的一小段映射。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consistent hashing maps keys and nodes onto a hash ring so adding or removing a node only reshuffles a small neighboring slice of the mapping.

optionExplanations: 按原计划给每个在线用户建节点，写路径会被百万级的上下线操作直接压垮，不是『扛得住』的问题。
对：只让服务器注册进 ZK、用户按一致性哈希映射到服务器，ZK 只管几十个节点，量级立刻可控。
单个 ZNode 要求小于 1MB，百万用户列表根本塞不进一个节点。
给每用户建 5 个节点只是把写压力再乘以 5，没解决量级过大这个根本问题，反而更糟。
optionExplanations_en: Sticking with per-user znodes means millions of connect/disconnect writes crush the write path — this is not something ZooKeeper can simply 'handle'.
Right: register only servers in ZooKeeper and hash users onto them by consistent hashing, so ZK only tracks a few dozen nodes and the scale stays manageable.
A single znode must stay under a megabyte — a million-user list cannot fit into one.
Five znodes per user just multiplies the write load by five; it does not fix the fundamental scale problem and actually makes it worse.

scenario: 要把 ZK 上线生产承载聊天集群的路由协调，任何一台机器宕机都不能让协调层停摆。
scenario_en: You are taking ZooKeeper to production to coordinate chat routing, and losing any single machine must not stop the coordination layer.
q: 生产环境的 ZooKeeper 部署形态是？
q_en: How should ZooKeeper be deployed in production?
options: 一台配置拉满的单一服务器，省去多机之间同步的麻烦，性能也绝对够用，部署起来还更省心
两台服务器做主备部署，一台挂了立刻切到另一台顶上
一组服务器（ensemble），典型 3、5 或 7 台——奇数便于多数派决策
至少需要上百台服务器组成一个超大规模的集群
options_en: One maxed-out single server, avoiding multi-machine sync overhead entirely, with plenty of performance and easy deployment.
Two servers in a primary-backup pair, failing over the moment one dies.
A group of servers, an ensemble, typically three, five, or seven — odd counts make majority decisions clean.
At least a hundred servers needed to form one giant cluster.
why: 单机是单点故障；ensemble 用奇数台便于形成多数派（quorum），只要多数存活集群就能工作。
why_en: ZooKeeper runs as an ensemble of typically three, five, or seven servers, since odd sizes make majority decisions cleaner.

termDefinitions.meaning: ensemble：ZooKeeper 集群里协同工作的一组服务器，共同对外提供一致视图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ensemble is the group of ZooKeeper servers that work together to provide one consistent view.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum（多数派）：ensemble 中过半数存活并达成一致的服务器数量，是继续对外服务的底线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the majority of ensemble servers that must be alive and agree before the cluster keeps serving.

optionExplanations: 单台服务器是典型的单点故障，一挂整个协调服务就没了，生产环境不会这么部署。
两台主备切换缺少多数派机制，网络分区时两边都可能自认为是主，容易脑裂。
对：典型部署是 3、5、7 台的 ensemble，奇数台便于凑出过半数，少数故障也能继续工作。
上百台不是必需的门槛，几台奇数服务器就足够容错，规模远没那么大。
optionExplanations_en: A single server is a textbook single point of failure — one crash takes down the whole coordination service, so production never deploys this way.
A two-server primary-backup pair has no majority mechanism, so during a partition both sides can believe they are primary — split-brain risk.
Right: a typical deployment is an ensemble of 3, 5, or 7 servers — odd counts make forming a majority clean, so a minority of failures does not stop the cluster.
A hundred servers is not the bar — a handful of odd-numbered servers is already enough for fault tolerance; the scale needed is nowhere near that.

scenario: 聊天集群的 ZK ensemble 有 5 台：路由读每秒上万次，写只在用户上下线时才发生。
scenario_en: The chat cluster's five-node ZooKeeper ensemble serves tens of thousands of routing reads per second, while writes happen only as users connect or disconnect.
q: ensemble 内部 Leader 和 Follower 的分工是？
q_en: How do the Leader and Followers split work inside a ZooKeeper ensemble?
options: Leader 处理所有更新（写）请求；Follower 跟随指令并帮助服务读请求，读可打到任意节点
Leader 平时只做冷备份，完全不参与任何读写请求的处理，只有其它所有节点都挂掉时才会顶上来接管
Follower 负责处理全部写请求，Leader 只负责处理读请求，两者角色正好反过来
所有节点角色完全平等，写请求随便打到哪台都行
options_en: The leader processes all writes; followers follow its instructions and help serve reads from any node.
The leader is just a cold standby that handles no reads or writes at all, stepping in only when every other node has failed.
Followers handle every write request while the leader only handles reads — the roles are flipped from normal.
All nodes are fully equal and a write can land on any server at random.
why: 写集中走 leader 保证全序；读可从任何节点读内存副本——这是 ZK 读多写少定位的架构基础。
why_en: The elected leader processes all writes while followers help serve reads from any server in the ensemble.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Leader"] --> B["Follower"]
  A --> C["Follower"]
  A --> D["Follower"]
  A --> E["Follower"]

termDefinitions.meaning: Leader：ensemble 中被选出、负责处理全部写请求并向 follower 广播变更的服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The leader is the elected server that processes all writes and broadcasts changes to followers.

termDefinitions.meaning: Follower：ensemble 中跟随 leader 指令、可对外提供读服务的其余服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Followers are the rest of the ensemble's servers that follow the leader and can serve reads.

optionExplanations: 对：leader 处理全部写请求并广播给 follower，follower 跟随并可以直接服务读请求，读可以打到任意节点。
leader 恰恰是最忙的那台：所有写都必须经过它并广播，绝不是闲置的冷备份。
写集中在 leader 才能保证全序，让 follower 各自处理写会立刻打破一致性。
写请求必须走 leader 才能排出全序，节点角色并不对等，随便打到哪台会破坏一致性保证。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the leader processes all writes and broadcasts them to followers, while followers follow along and can directly serve reads from any node.
The leader is in fact the busiest node: every write must pass through it and be broadcast — it is never an idle cold standby.
Writes are concentrated at the leader precisely to keep a total order; letting followers handle writes would break consistency immediately.
Writes must go through the leader to establish a total order — the roles are not equal, and scattering writes anywhere would break the consistency guarantee.

scenario: 聊天平台要求即便同时有服务器故障，路由用的 ZooKeeper ensemble 依然能继续处理读写；团队把 ensemble 定为 5 台。
scenario_en: The chat platform needs its ZooKeeper ensemble to keep serving routing reads and writes even when some servers fail. The team chooses a 5-node ensemble.
q: 5 台服务器的 ZooKeeper ensemble 最多能容忍几台故障仍正常工作？
q_en: In a 5-node ZooKeeper ensemble, how many node failures can it tolerate?
options: 1 台，因为多一台都会丢失多数派
2 台，因为剩下的 3 台仍是多数派（quorum）
3 台，只要还剩 2 台在线，理论上就能继续工作，风险可以接受
4 台，只要还有 1 台在线就能工作
options_en: One, because losing a second server would break the majority.
Two, because the remaining three servers still form a quorum majority.
Three, as long as two servers stay online, which should be an acceptable risk.
Four, as long as one server stays online.
why: 容忍故障数 = ⌈N/2⌉-1；5 台的多数派门槛是 3 台，所以最多能失去 2 台。这个门槛也是选 3/5/7 奇数 ensemble 的原因。
why_en: A five-server ensemble tolerates two failures because three remaining servers still form a majority, or quorum.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum（多数派）：ensemble 里过半数服务器，是继续接受写请求的最低存活门槛。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the majority of ensemble servers that must stay alive for the cluster to keep accepting writes.

scenario: 聊天服务器要连一个 3 节点 ZK ensemble，任何一台 ZK 宕机时业务连接都不能中断。
scenario_en: A chat server connects to a three-node ZooKeeper ensemble and must keep its session alive even when one node goes down.
q: 客户端连接 ZooKeeper 时的连接串长什么样？为什么？
q_en: What does a ZooKeeper client connection string look like, and why?
options: 只填当前 leader 那一台服务器的地址，其余 follower 地址客户端完全不需要知道，断连了也不用自己管重连，配置更简单省心，反正读写都由 leader 兜着
填一个统一的负载均衡器地址，把连哪台 ZooKeeper 的决定权完全交给负载均衡器
填整个 ensemble 的地址列表（如 zk1:2181,zk2:2181,zk3:2181）+ 会话超时 + watcher 回调
只填一个 DNS 泛域名地址，具体解析到哪台机器完全交给 DNS 服务去决定
options_en: Only the current leader's address; the client need not know any followers and never handles reconnects — simpler config, since the leader covers all reads and writes anyway.
A unified load balancer address, leaving which ZooKeeper server to route to entirely up to it.
The full ensemble address list plus a session timeout and a watcher callback.
Just a wildcard DNS name, leaving which machine gets resolved entirely up to DNS.
why: 客户端知道全部节点，某台挂了可以换一台重连并恢复会话；构造参数里还有会话超时和 watch 回调。
why_en: Clients connect with the full ensemble address list plus a session timeout and watcher callback, so any live server can serve them.
codeSample:
// Chat Server 1 连接 ZooKeeper
ZooKeeper zk = new ZooKeeper(
  "zk1:2181,zk2:2181,zk3:2181", // 全部 ensemble 地址
  3000,     // 会话超时（毫秒）
  watcher); // 变更通知回调

termDefinitions.meaning: ensemble：客户端连接串里列出的一组 ZooKeeper 服务器地址，任一台存活即可接入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ensemble is the set of ZooKeeper server addresses in the connection string; any live one can serve the client.

termDefinitions.meaning: watcher：客户端注册的回调函数，节点变化时由 ZooKeeper 主动调用通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A watcher is a client-registered callback that ZooKeeper invokes when a watched node changes.

optionExplanations: 只知道 leader 地址的话，一旦 leader 换人或挂掉，客户端就无处重连、恢复不了会话。
ZooKeeper 客户端库自己管理连接和故障转移，不需要额外一层负载均衡器来决定连哪台。
对：连接串带上全部 ensemble 地址加会话超时和 watcher 回调，某台挂了客户端能自己换一台重连。
泛域名把解析权交给 DNS，DNS 缓存和刷新的滞后会让客户端连到已经不可用的节点。
optionExplanations_en: Knowing only the leader address means that once the leader changes or dies, the client has nowhere to reconnect and cannot recover its session.
The ZooKeeper client library already manages connections and failover itself — it does not need an extra load balancer deciding which server to hit.
Right: the connection string lists the full ensemble plus a session timeout and watcher callback, so if one server dies the client can reconnect to another itself.
A wildcard DNS name hands resolution to DNS, and DNS caching/refresh lag can point the client at a server that is already down.

scenario: 聊天服务器要在 Bob 换服务器的瞬间知道路由变了，又不想每秒都去 ZK 轮询一遍。
scenario_en: A chat server needs to know the instant Bob's routing changes, without polling ZooKeeper every second to find out.
q: watch 机制是什么？
q_en: What is the ZooKeeper watch mechanism?
options: 客户端本地定时轮询 ZNode 状态的一个定时器
在 ZNode 上登记的一次性通知：节点变化时 ZK 主动回调客户端，免去持续轮询
ZooKeeper 自带的运维监控大盘，展示集群健康状态
客户端与 ZooKeeper 建立连接时用的一种加密握手协议，和后续数据变化没有关系
options_en: A local timer on the client that periodically polls a znode's state.
A one-time notification registered on a znode: ZooKeeper calls the client back when it changes, replacing constant polling.
ZooKeeper's built-in ops dashboard showing cluster health.
An encryption handshake protocol used when a client connects to ZooKeeper, unrelated to later data changes.
why: watch 把「拉」变「推」：关心某数据的服务器被动接收变更通知，不用每次都查询 ZK。
why_en: A watch notifies the client when a znode changes, replacing constant polling with push notifications.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant Z as ZooKeeper
  C->>Z: read znode with watch
  Z-->>C: data
  Z-->>C: change event
  C->>Z: re-read and re-watch

termDefinitions.meaning: watch：客户端在读取 ZNode 时顺带登记的一次性变更通知，触发后需要重新设置才能继续监听。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A watch is a one-time change notification registered while reading a znode; it must be re-armed after it fires.

optionExplanations: 定时轮询是 watch 出现之前的笨办法，客户端得不停发请求才能发现变化。
对：watch 是在 ZNode 上登记的一次性通知，节点变化时 ZooKeeper 主动回调客户端，省掉持续轮询。
监控大盘是运维可视化工具，和这个『节点变化时通知客户端』的机制完全是两回事。
加密握手发生在建立连接阶段，watch 是数据变化后的推送机制，二者不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Polling on a timer is the clunky pre-watch approach — the client has to keep asking just to notice a change.
Right: a watch is a one-time notification registered on a znode; ZooKeeper calls the client back when it changes, replacing constant polling.
An ops dashboard is a visualization tool — completely different from a mechanism that notifies a client when a node changes.
An encryption handshake happens at connection setup; a watch is a push notification after data changes — different concerns.

scenario: 聊天集群每秒转发数千条消息，每条都直接查一次 ZK 拿收件人所在的服务器地址。
scenario_en: The chat cluster forwards thousands of messages per second and hits ZooKeeper for the recipient's server address on every one of them.
q: 如果没有 watch，每发一条消息都查一次 ZK 拿路由，会发生什么？
q_en: What happens if every message queries ZooKeeper for routing instead of using watches?
options: 消息会因为查询顺序问题而乱序到达
ZooKeeper 会自动检测到压力并无缝扩容出更多节点
没有明显影响，因为 ZooKeeper 的读性能理论上没有上限
显著延迟 + ZK 被每秒数千次查询压垮，协调服务自己变成瓶颈
options_en: Messages would arrive out of order because of query timing.
ZooKeeper automatically detects the load and scales itself out seamlessly.
No real impact, since ZooKeeper's read throughput is effectively unbounded.
Noticeable latency plus thousands of queries per second overwhelm the cluster, turning the coordinator into the bottleneck.
why: ZK 是协调服务不是高吞吐读库；正确姿势是本地缓存 + watch 通知更新缓存。
why_en: Querying ZooKeeper per message adds latency and crushes the cluster, so you cache locally and rely on watch notifications instead.
optionExplanations: 查询顺序和消息到达顺序是两件不相关的事，这不是每次查库会造成的问题。
ZooKeeper 不会自动检测压力并无缝扩容，它是需要手动规划容量的协调服务。
ZooKeeper 的读吞吐并非无限，每秒数千次查询照样会把它压垮，不是『没有影响』。
对：每条消息都现查会叠加延迟，同时把每秒数千次请求压到协调服务头上，让 ZK 自己变成瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Query timing and message arrival order are unrelated — that is not what per-message querying actually breaks.
ZooKeeper does not auto-detect load and scale itself out — it is a coordination service that needs capacity planned manually.
ZooKeeper's read throughput is not unbounded — thousands of queries per second will still overwhelm it, so 'no impact' is wrong.
Right: querying per message stacks up latency and dumps thousands of requests per second onto the coordination service, turning it into the bottleneck itself.

scenario: 聊天服务器要以内存级延迟拿到路由，同时保证用户迁移后几十毫秒内就能纠正过来。
scenario_en: Chat servers want routing lookups at memory speed, yet must self-correct within tens of milliseconds after a user migrates.
q: watch 支撑的关键使用模式是？
q_en: What key usage pattern do ZooKeeper watches enable?
options: 每次要读数据都实时发一次请求查 ZooKeeper，不做任何缓存，也不关心 watch 机制
服务器保留一份 ZK 状态的本地缓存，平时读本地；数据变化时收到通知再更新缓存
把 ZooKeeper 直接当消息队列，用它转发聊天消息本体
watch 触发后会把变化的数据自动同步写进后端数据库
options_en: Send a fresh request to ZooKeeper for every read, with no local caching at all, and no concern for the watch mechanism.
Keep a local cache of ZooKeeper state, read from it locally, and update it on watch notifications.
Treat ZooKeeper as a message queue and forward chat message bodies through it.
A watch firing automatically syncs the changed data straight into a backend database.
why: 「本地缓存 + 变更通知」是 ZK 的标准用法：读走本地内存，一致性靠 watch 回调维护。
why_en: Servers keep a local cache of ZooKeeper state and update it on watch notifications instead of querying every time.
optionExplanations: 完全不做缓存意味着每次读都要跨网络问 ZK，这正是要靠 watch 避免的低效模式。
对：服务器保留一份 ZK 状态的本地缓存，平时读本地内存，数据变化时靠 watch 通知再更新缓存。
ZooKeeper 不是拿来转发消息本体的消息队列，那是 Kafka 之类系统该干的事。
watch 触发的是客户端回调，不会自动把数据写进后端数据库，那需要客户端自己去做。
optionExplanations_en: Never caching means every read crosses the network to ZooKeeper — exactly the inefficiency watches exist to avoid.
Right: servers keep a local cache of ZooKeeper state, read from memory locally, and refresh it on watch notifications when data changes.
ZooKeeper is not a message queue for forwarding payloads — that job belongs to something like Kafka.
A watch firing just triggers the client's callback — it does not automatically write into a backend database; the client has to do that itself.

scenario: 有人想把聊天应用的用户资料和消息历史也塞进 ZK，理由是「反正它也能存数据」。
scenario_en: Someone wants to keep user profiles and message history in ZooKeeper too, on the grounds that it stores data anyway.
q: 为什么说 ZooKeeper 是「协调服务」而不是「数据库」？
q_en: Why is ZooKeeper a coordination service rather than a database?
options: 因为它的数据不支持持久化，重启后就会丢失全部内容
因为它根本没有任何查询语言或读取接口，客户端连把存进去的数据读出来都做不到
它的设计目标是把变更通知给各系统，而不是承接高流量读请求
因为它只能存字符串类型，不支持存放数字或二进制数据
options_en: Because its data is not durable and everything disappears after a restart.
Because it has no query language or read interface at all, so clients cannot even read back the data they stored.
It is built to notify systems of changes, not to serve high-volume read traffic.
Because it can only store strings and cannot hold numbers or binary data.
why: ZK 的价值在一致视图 + 变更通知；高频读写请自备缓存或换存储，别把它当 KV 数据库用。
why_en: ZooKeeper is built to notify systems of changes, not to serve high-volume read traffic like a database.
tradeoff: 变更通知型协调服务（低吞吐、强一致视图）vs 高吞吐读写数据库（大数据量、无内置推送）
optionExplanations: ZK 的数据是持久化的，重启不会丢，这不是它和数据库的区别所在。
ZooKeeper 有自己的读写 API（get/set/getChildren），能读能写，只是不是 SQL，不是完全没有查询能力。
对：ZK 的定位是把变更通知给各系统，而不是承接高流量读请求，这才是它区别于数据库的关键。
ZNode 能存字节数据，不限于字符串，这也不是这道题真正的区分点。
optionExplanations_en: ZooKeeper's data is durable and survives restarts — that is not what separates it from a database.
ZooKeeper has its own read/write API (get/set/getChildren) — it can read and write, just not via SQL, so it is not query-less.
Right: ZooKeeper is built to notify systems of changes rather than serve high-volume read traffic — that is what actually distinguishes it from a database.
A znode can hold arbitrary byte data, not just strings, so that is not the real distinction here either.

scenario: Server 1 想在「任何用户的位置变化」时收到通知并更新自己的路由表。
scenario_en: Server 1 wants to be notified whenever any user location changes so it can update its local routing table.
q: 正确的做法是？
q_en: What is the correct way to use watches for routing changes?
options: zk.getChildren("/chat-app/users", true, null) 注册 watch，回调里读新值并更新路由表
每隔 100ms 用一个本地轮询定时器主动查询一次 /chat-app/users 整个目录，不管有没有变化都拉一遍，实现起来也很直观，还不用注册任何回调
让 Server 1 额外去订阅一个独立的 Kafka topic，专门转发用户位置变化事件
让每台服务器之间持续互相发送心跳探测包，顺带在心跳里夹带用户位置信息
options_en: Register a watch with zk.getChildren on /chat-app/users, then read and update the routing table in the callback.
Use a local polling timer to query the whole /chat-app/users path every 100 ms whether or not anything changed — straightforward to implement, with no callback to register.
Have Server 1 additionally subscribe to a separate Kafka topic dedicated to forwarding location changes.
Have every server continuously exchange heartbeat probes with each other, piggybacking user location on them.
why: getChildren/getData 的 watch 参数登记监听；回调触发后读取新数据、更新本地缓存并再次设置 watch。
why_en: Register a watch on the users path and update the local routing table in the callback when a znode changes.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要一次性读取而不关心后续变化，不带 watch 的普通读取即可。
tradeoff: watch 推送更新（事件触发、零轮询开销）vs 定时轮询（简单但延迟高、浪费请求）

termDefinitions.meaning: getChildren：读取某个 ZNode 下所有子节点列表的 API，第二个参数传 true 即同时注册 watch。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: getChildren reads the list of a znode's children; passing true also registers a watch on that path.

termDefinitions.meaning: getData：读取某个 ZNode 数据内容的 API，同样可以顺带注册 watch。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: getData reads a znode's data content and can also register a watch on it.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka：一个分布式消息队列/流处理系统，用于高吞吐地传输事件流，不是协调服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed messaging and stream-processing system for high-throughput event streams, not a coordination service.

optionExplanations: 对：把 getChildren 的第二个参数设成 true 就等于登记了监听，之后变化才触发一次回调、读取新值更新路由表，空闲时零开销。
固定 100ms 轮询无论有没有变化都发请求，既浪费带宽，延迟又比事件触发的 watch 更高。
额外接一个 Kafka topic 是多引入一整套消息系统，而 ZK 的 watch 本来就能做到同样的事。
心跳的频率通常比位置变化慢得多，夹带数据会让路由更新明显滞后。
optionExplanations_en: Right: register a watch via getChildren, so only a real change fires a callback that reads the new value and updates the routing table, costing nothing while idle.
Fixed 100 ms polling fires requests whether or not anything changed — it wastes bandwidth and has higher latency than an event-driven watch.
Bolting on a separate Kafka topic adds a whole extra messaging system when ZooKeeper's watch already does the same job.
Heartbeat cadence is usually much slower than location changes, so piggybacking on it would make routing updates noticeably stale.

scenario: 聊天平台要盘点 ZK 能接管哪些协调职责：动态限速参数、服务器名单、单一协调者、互斥。
scenario_en: The chat platform is taking stock of which coordination duties ZooKeeper can absorb: dynamic rate limits, the server roster, a single coordinator, and mutual exclusion.
q: ZooKeeper 的四大核心用途是？（多选）
q_en: What are ZooKeeper's four core use cases? (Select all that apply.)
options: 配置管理（Configuration Management）
服务发现（Service Discovery）
Leader 选举与分布式锁
全文搜索（Full-text Search）
options_en: Configuration management
Service discovery
Leader election and distributed locks
Full-text search
why: 配置管理、服务发现、leader 选举、分布式锁——四大能力都是「ZNode + 临时/顺序节点 + watch」三件套的组合应用。
why_en: ZooKeeper's four main capabilities are configuration management, service discovery, leader election, and distributed locks.
optionExplanations: 配置管理靠一个小 ZNode + watch 推送，改一次全体服务器秒级感知，不用重启。
服务发现靠临时节点自动注册/下线，调用方读子节点列表并 watch 就能拿到实时的可用实例。
leader 选举和分布式锁都建立在顺序+临时节点上：序号最小者当选/持锁，前任消失才轮到下一个。
全文搜索需要倒排索引和大规模文本存储，ZNode 只放小量协调数据，不是它的活。
optionExplanations_en: Configuration management runs on a small znode plus watch push — one update reaches every server in seconds, no restart needed.
Service discovery relies on ephemeral nodes auto-registering and vanishing, so callers just read the children and watch for live instances.
Leader election and distributed locks both build on sequential ephemeral nodes: lowest number wins or holds, and the next in line takes over when it disappears.
Full-text search needs an inverted index and bulk text storage — znodes only hold small coordination data, not this job.

scenario: 要给整个聊天平台上线一个新功能开关，希望所有服务器实时生效、不用重启。
scenario_en: You need to launch a new feature flag across the chat platform, and every server should see it in real time without a restart.
q: 用 ZooKeeper 怎么做？
q_en: How would you implement this with ZooKeeper?
options: SSH 逐台登录到每一台服务器，手动修改本地配置文件后再滚动重启服务进程，耗时又容易漏改，规模一大根本忙不过来，还没法保证每台机器改得一致
更新一个 ZNode（如 enable_reactions 设为 true），watch 该节点的服务器收到通知后即时改变行为
给运维和研发团队群发一封全员邮件，逐个通知大家自行手动修改本地配置
把开关值直接硬编码进代码常量里面，走一次完整的重新打包和发布上线流程
options_en: SSH into each server one by one, manually edit the local config file, then rolling-restart the process — slow, error-prone, unmanageable at scale, and no guarantee every machine ends up consistent.
Update one znode (say, enable_reactions to true) and every watching server reacts instantly.
Send an all-hands email to ops and engineering, telling everyone to manually change their local config one by one.
Hard-code the flag as a constant right in the code and go through a full rebuild-and-redeploy cycle.
why: 集中配置 + watch 通知 = 实时传播、版本化、原子更新；这是 ZK 配置管理的招牌场景。
why_en: Update one znode and every watching server gets notified and changes behavior without restarting.
whenOtherWins: 只在部署时才变的静态配置放文件或环境变量更合适；云上可用 AWS Parameter Store / Azure App Configuration 等托管方案。
tradeoff: 集中 ZNode + watch 推送（秒级生效、免重启）vs 改文件重启（简单但要停机滚动）
codeSample:
# 更新配置节点
set /chat-app/config/enable_reactions "true"

# 所有 watch 该路径的服务器收到 NodeDataChanged 事件
# 在回调里读取新值、切换功能开关，无需重启
optionExplanations: 逐台 SSH 改配置再重启，既慢又容易漏改、还难保证一致，和『实时生效、不重启』的要求正相反。
对：更新一个 ZNode，所有 watch 它的服务器立刻收到通知并在回调里切换行为，秒级生效且不用重启。
群发邮件靠人工手动改配置，既不实时也不可靠，规模一大根本跟不上。
硬编码进代码常量意味着每次开关都要走一次完整的重新打包发布，远谈不上『实时』。
optionExplanations_en: SSHing into each box to edit and restart is slow, error-prone, and hard to keep consistent — the opposite of instant, restart-free updates.
Right: update one znode and every watching server gets notified instantly and flips behavior in its callback, live and without a restart.
An all-hands email relies on people manually editing config — neither real-time nor reliable, and it does not scale.
Hard-coding the flag as a constant means every toggle needs a full rebuild-and-redeploy cycle — far from real-time.

scenario: 聊天应用有两类配置：限速阈值要在运行时改，数据库连接串只在部署时才变。
scenario_en: The chat app has two kinds of config: rate-limit thresholds that must change at runtime, and a database connection string that only changes at deploy time.
q: 哪类配置适合放 ZooKeeper，哪类不适合？
q_en: Which configuration belongs in ZooKeeper, and which does not?
options: 所有配置不论是否会变，一律放进 ZooKeeper 统一管理，图个省心不做区分
所有配置都硬编码进代码里，靠重新发布来更新
ZooKeeper 只用来存密码这类敏感信息，其它都不放
运行时可能变化的动态配置放 ZK；只在部署时变化的静态配置放文件或环境变量
options_en: Put every config value in ZooKeeper regardless of whether it ever changes, just to keep things simple and uniform.
Hard-code every config value into the code and rely on redeploys to change it.
Only put secrets like passwords in ZooKeeper and keep everything else out.
Put runtime-changeable dynamic config in ZooKeeper; keep deploy-time static config in files or environment variables.
why: ZK 的价值在「变化时的实时传播」；不变的东西放文件/环境变量成本更低。云上优先考虑 provider 原生方案。
why_en: Put dynamic runtime configuration in ZooKeeper and keep static deploy-time configuration in files or environment variables.
tradeoff: 动态配置走 ZK（实时推送，多一次网络依赖）vs 静态配置放文件/环境变量（零依赖，改了要重新部署）
optionExplanations: 静态不变的配置也塞进 ZK，只是多了一次网络依赖，没有换来任何好处。
全部硬编码意味着连该实时生效的动态开关也要走一次重新发布，失去了 ZK 的价值。
把 ZK 局限成只存密码低估了它的用途，动态路由、开关这些也该放进去。
对：运行时会变的动态配置放 ZK 换实时推送，只在部署时变的静态配置放文件/环境变量，成本更低。
optionExplanations_en: Putting even static, never-changing config in ZooKeeper just adds a network dependency with no real benefit.
Hard-coding everything means even config that should update live needs a redeploy, throwing away ZooKeeper's whole value.
Limiting ZooKeeper to secrets alone undersells it — dynamic routing and flags belong there too.
Right: put config that changes at runtime in ZooKeeper for live push, and keep config that only changes at deploy time in files or environment variables, which is cheaper.

scenario: 微服务架构：上传服务要找到当前可用的视频转码器实例，实例随时扩缩容和故障。
scenario_en: In a microservice architecture, the upload service must find currently available video transcoder instances as they scale up, scale down, and fail.
q: 用 ZooKeeper 的标准做法是？
q_en: What is the standard ZooKeeper pattern for service discovery?
options: 把转码器的 IP 列表写死在上传服务的配置文件里
上传服务每次调用前先 ping 一遍所有可能的转码器 IP，确认对方还活着再发请求
转码器实例注册临时节点；调用方读子节点列表选一个连接，并设 watch 感知实例增减
让转码器实例反过来主动轮询上传服务，报告自己是否空闲
options_en: Hard-code the transcoder IP list into the upload service's config file.
Have the upload service ping every possible transcoder IP before each call to confirm it is still alive.
Transcoder instances register ephemeral nodes; the caller reads the children and watches for changes.
Have transcoder instances poll the upload service to report whether they are free.
why: 服务上线注册（临时节点）、下线自动消失（会话过期）、调用方 watch 子节点列表——动态扩缩容、负载均衡、健康检查一举拿下。
why_en: Instances register ephemeral nodes, consumers read the children to pick one, and a watch keeps the list current as instances come and go.
whenOtherWins: 现代栈里 Consul、etcd、Kubernetes Service、AWS Cloud Map 等专用/平台方案更常见——模式与 ZK 一致，有些内部甚至就用 ZK。
tradeoff: 动态注册+watch（自动感知扩缩容）vs 静态写死 IP（简单但扩缩容要改配置重发）
optionExplanations: IP 写死在配置文件里，转码器一扩缩容配置就过期，得手动改配置重发才能跟上。
每次调用前逐个 ping 一遍会叠加探测延迟，而且探测结果可能在真正使用前就已经过期。
对：转码器注册临时节点，调用方读子节点列表并设 watch，新实例秒级可见、崩溃实例自动消失。
反过来让转码器轮询上传服务，上传服务失去主动权，还得多维护一套反向汇报协议。
optionExplanations_en: Hard-coded IPs in a config file go stale the moment transcoders scale up or down — someone has to manually edit and redeploy to catch up.
Pinging every possible instance before each call adds probing latency, and the result can already be stale by the time it is used.
Right: transcoders register ephemeral nodes and callers read the children with a watch, so new instances show up in seconds and crashed ones vanish automatically.
Flipping it so transcoders poll the upload service takes away the caller's control and forces you to maintain a whole reverse reporting protocol.

q: 把 ZooKeeper 的应用级 leader 选举配方排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put ZooKeeper's application-level leader election recipe in the correct order.
steps: 序号最小的服务器成为 leader
每台服务器在指定路径下创建顺序+临时节点
leader 故障 → 它的节点消失，下一个序号的服务器收到通知接任
其余服务器各自 watch「比自己小的下一个序号」的节点
why: 创建顺序临时节点 → 最小序号当 leader → 各自 watch 前一个 → 前面的消失就接班。自动故障转移，同一时刻只有一个 leader。
why_en: Each server creates a sequential ephemeral node, the lowest number leads, everyone watches the next lower node, and when the leader dies the next in line takes over.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    A["node-0001 (leader)"] -.被 watch.- B["node-0002"]
    B -.被 watch.- C["node-0003"]
    A -- 崩溃消失 --> B2["node-0002 成为新 leader"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序+临时节点：同时具备顺序节点的递增编号和临时节点的会话绑定特性，是选举与锁配方的原料。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequential ephemeral node combines an auto-incrementing suffix with session-bound auto-deletion, the building block for election and lock recipes.

scenario: 100 台聊天服务器用顺序临时节点排队抢 leader，要避免每次退位就惊醒全体（惊群）。
scenario_en: A hundred chat servers queue for leadership using sequential ephemeral nodes, and you must avoid waking every one of them each time the leader steps down.
q: 选举配方里，为什么 Server 3 watch 的是 node-0000000002（前一个），而不是 leader 的 node-0000000001？
q_en: In the election recipe, why does Server 3 watch node-0000000002 instead of the leader node?
options: watch leader 节点是为了持续监控它的 CPU 和内存性能
两种 watch 方式在效果上完全等价，选哪个都可以
因为单个客户端在 ZooKeeper 上能注册的 watch 数量有硬性上限
链式监听：每人只盯前一位，任何节点消失只惊动它的下一位，通知量最小
options_en: Watching the leader's node is meant to monitor its CPU and memory usage.
The two watch strategies are functionally equivalent, so either works fine.
There is a hard cap on how many watches a single client can register.
A chain: each server watches only the next lower node, so a failure notifies exactly one successor.
why: 链式 watch 让每次变动只通知一个等待者，避免全体涌向同一节点；谁的前任消失谁递补。
why_en: Each server watches only the next lower node, forming a chain so a failure notifies exactly one successor instead of everyone.
optionExplanations: watch 只是登记『节点变化时通知我』，不会拿来持续监控 CPU、内存这类性能指标。
两种 watch 方式效果并不等价：全体盯 leader 会让 leader 消失时所有人同时被唤醒。
单客户端能注册的 watch 数量不是这里的限制因素，链式设计的目的是控制通知量。
对：每人只盯自己前一位，一个节点消失只会惊动它的下一位，通知量降到最小，避免全员同时被唤醒。
optionExplanations_en: A watch just registers 'notify me on change' — it is not used to continuously monitor CPU or memory metrics.
The two watch strategies are not equivalent: if everyone watched the leader, its disappearance would wake everyone at once.
A per-client watch cap is not the limiting factor here — the chain design exists to control notification volume.
Right: each server watches only the node just before it, so one disappearance wakes exactly its successor, keeping notifications minimal and avoiding a thundering herd.

scenario: 要说服团队采用「最小顺序节点当 leader」这套配方，得先举出生产级系统的真实先例。
scenario_en: To convince your team to adopt the smallest-sequential-node election recipe, you first need real production systems that actually shipped it.
q: 哪些真实系统用过 ZooKeeper 的这种 leader 选举模式？
q_en: Which real systems have used this ZooKeeper leader election pattern?
options: HBase 的 schema 变更协调，以及早期 Kafka 用它选出管理分区领导权的 controller broker
Redis 的主从故障切换机制，同样是靠这套顺序临时节点选举模式挑出新的主节点，只是换了个产品名字而已，底层本质完全一样，可以直接照搬
Nginx 做请求负载均衡的时候，也是用它在多个后端实例间选一个当前活跃节点
Git 在合并多个分支的时候，也是用它决定哪一条分支的提交历史应该优先保留
options_en: HBase's schema-change coordination, and early Kafka's controller broker that manages partition leadership.
Redis master-slave failover also uses this same sequential ephemeral-node election to pick a new master — just a different product name, fundamentally identical, directly transferable.
Nginx also uses it to elect one active backend instance among several for request load balancing.
Git also uses it to decide which branch's commit history should be kept as priority during a merge.
why: HBase 靠它保证一台服务器协调 schema 变更；KRaft 之前的 Kafka 用它选 controller——经典的「同一时刻只有一个人干关键活」。
why_en: HBase coordinates schema changes and pre-KRaft Kafka elected its controller broker using this ZooKeeper pattern.

termDefinitions.meaning: HBase：构建在 Hadoop 之上的分布式列式数据库，历史上用 ZooKeeper 做协调。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HBase is a distributed column-family database built on Hadoop that has historically used ZooKeeper for coordination.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka：分布式消息队列/事件流平台，早期版本依赖 ZooKeeper 管理集群元数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed messaging and event-streaming platform whose early versions relied on ZooKeeper for cluster metadata.

termDefinitions.meaning: controller broker：Kafka 集群中被选出、专门负责管理分区 leader 分配的那台 broker。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The controller broker is the elected Kafka broker responsible for managing partition leader assignment.

optionExplanations: 对：HBase 用它协调 schema 变更，Kafka 在采用 KRaft 之前也靠它选出负责分区管理的 controller broker。
Redis 主从切换靠自己的 Sentinel/Cluster 投票机制，不依赖 ZooKeeper 这套临时节点选举配方。
Nginx 是无状态的请求转发，负载均衡算法里没有『谁是 leader』这个概念。
Git 合并靠提交图和合并策略，是版本控制层面的操作，和运行时协调服务不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Right: HBase coordinates schema changes with it, and pre-KRaft Kafka used it to elect the controller broker managing partitions.
Redis failover relies on its own Sentinel/Cluster voting, not on this ZooKeeper ephemeral-node election recipe.
Nginx is stateless request forwarding — its load-balancing algorithm has no notion of 'who is the leader'.
Git merging relies on commit graphs and merge strategies, a version-control operation unrelated to runtime coordination.

scenario: 多个支付 worker 都想处理同一笔 payment，但同一时刻只能有一个 worker 进入临界区。worker 可能崩溃，所以锁必须能自动释放。
scenario_en: Multiple payment workers want to process the same payment, but only one worker may enter the critical section at a time. Workers can crash, so the lock must release automatically.
q: ZooKeeper 分布式锁的配方是？
q_en: What is the ZooKeeper distributed-lock recipe?
options: 所有客户端抢写同一个固定节点，成功者持锁
每个客户端建临时顺序节点，最小号持锁
由 ensemble leader 手动挑一个客户端发锁
按客户端本地时间戳排序，最早者持锁
options_en: All clients race to write the same fixed node; whoever succeeds holds the lock.
Each client creates an ephemeral sequential node; the lowest number holds the lock.
The ensemble leader manually chooses one client and grants the lock.
Sort by each client's local timestamp; the earliest one holds the lock.
why: 把锁想成排队拿号：每个客户端拿一个会自动递增、会话结束会消失的节点号。号最小的人持锁；其他人只 watch 自己前一个号，前一个消失后再检查是否轮到自己。
why_en: Think of the lock as taking a queue ticket: each client creates an ephemeral sequential node, the lowest ticket holds the lock, and everyone else watches only the previous ticket.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是同一进程内互斥，用本地 mutex；如果是高频短锁，Redis 或数据库条件写通常更轻。
tradeoff: 公平排队+崩溃自动释放 vs 每次加解锁都走 ZooKeeper 写路径
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["Client creates lock-0007"] --> B["List lock queue"]
  B --> C{"Am I smallest?"}
  C -->|"yes"| D["Enter critical section"]
  C -->|"no"| E["Watch lock-0006"]
  E --> F["0006 deleted or session expired"]
  F --> B

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一时刻只能由一个 worker 执行的代码段，例如处理同一笔 payment。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A critical section is code that only one worker may execute at a time, such as processing one payment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 临时顺序节点：名字带递增编号，创建者会话结束时自动删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ephemeral sequential node has an increasing suffix and is deleted when its creator session ends.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只监听自己前一个排队节点。这样释放锁时只唤醒下一位，避免全部等待者一起抢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Watching the predecessor means listening only to the queue node just before yours, so only the next waiter wakes.

optionExplanations: 大家争同一个固定节点确实能选出赢家，但锁释放时所有等待者会一起被唤醒抢，形成惊群。
对：每个客户端建一个临时顺序节点，号最小的持锁，其余人只 watch 自己前一位，前一位消失或崩溃就自动轮到下一个。
ensemble leader 负责的是内部共识写入，不会替业务层去手动挑人发锁，这混淆了两个不同的角色。
各机器本地时钟会漂移，用时间戳排序得不到可靠的全局顺序，谁先谁后说不准。
optionExplanations_en: Racing on one fixed node can pick a winner, but releasing it wakes every waiter at once — a stampede.
Right: each client creates an ephemeral sequential node, the lowest number holds the lock, and everyone else watches only their predecessor so a crash or release wakes exactly the next one.
The ensemble leader handles internal consensus writes — it does not manually hand out application-level locks; that conflates two different roles.
Local clocks drift across machines, so ordering by timestamp gives no reliable global order — you cannot trust who was really first.

scenario: 库存扣减服务每秒要加解锁数百次，每次持锁只有几毫秒，跑在 5 节点 ZK 上。
scenario_en: An inventory service acquires and releases a lock hundreds of times per second, holding it only a few milliseconds, on a five-node ZooKeeper ensemble.
q: ZooKeeper 锁不适合什么场景？该用什么替代？
q_en: When is a ZooKeeper lock a poor fit, and what should replace it?
options: 只要持锁时间超过几分钟，就应该换成本地内存锁替代
任何生产场景都不该用 ZooKeeper 锁，风险太高
高频加解锁（每秒数百次）；这种场景考虑 Redis 锁或数据库事务
跨机房部署的场景不适合，应该改成让每个机房各自独立维护一套互不协调的本地锁
options_en: Any hold time over a few minutes should switch to a local in-memory lock.
ZooKeeper locks should never be used in any production scenario at all.
High-frequency locking, hundreds of times per second, where Redis locks or database transactions fit better.
It is unfit for cross-datacenter deployments; each datacenter should instead keep its own independent, uncoordinated local lock.
why: 每次加解锁都是走共识的写操作，高频场景撑不住；高频轻量锁交给 Redis 或数据库。
why_en: ZooKeeper locks are not built for hundreds of acquisitions per second, where Redis locks or database transactions fit better.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 锁：用 SETNX/TTL 等 Redis 命令实现的轻量分布式锁，吞吐高但依赖超时管理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis lock is a lightweight distributed lock built with commands like SETNX and TTL, offering high throughput but relying on timeout management.

optionExplanations: 持锁几分钟以上恰恰不是问题——ZK 锁擅长这种长持有场景，本地内存锁反而解决不了跨进程互斥。
『任何生产场景都不该用』太绝对，长持有、正确性优先的场景 ZK 锁正是合适的选择。
对：每次加解锁都是一次要走共识的写操作，每秒数百次的高频场景撑不住，该换 Redis 锁或数据库事务。
跨机房本身不是 ZK 锁的禁区，真正的限制是加解锁频率太高，不是地理分布。
optionExplanations_en: A hold time of a few minutes or more is not the problem — ZK locks are actually good at long holds; a local in-memory lock cannot even give cross-process mutual exclusion.
'Never use it in production' is too absolute — for long-held, correctness-first scenarios a ZK lock is exactly the right choice.
Right: every lock acquire and release is a consensus write, which cannot keep up at hundreds of times per second — that is when Redis locks or database transactions fit better.
Cross-datacenter use is not off-limits for ZK locks; the real limit is too-high lock/unlock frequency, not geography.

scenario: 金融交易的关键操作需要分布式锁：正确性压倒性能，锁可能持有数小时，持锁进程崩溃必须被可靠检测。
scenario_en: A financial transaction workflow needs a distributed lock. Correctness matters more than throughput, the lock may be held for hours, and a crashed holder must be detected reliably.
q: 选 ZooKeeper 锁还是 Redis 锁？
q_en: Should you choose a ZooKeeper lock or a Redis lock?
options: ZooKeeper 锁：一致性更强，临时节点自动检测崩溃，长锁不用小心翼翼管超时
Redis 锁：吞吐更高、延迟更低，看起来很适合这种长时间持有的场景，团队也更熟悉
两者随便选一个都可以，反正最终业务结果都是一样的
干脆不加锁，靠业务失败之后重试来兜底数据一致性
options_en: ZooKeeper locks: stronger consistency, ephemeral nodes auto-detect crashes, no fragile timeout tuning for long holds.
Redis locks — higher throughput and lower latency, which looks like a fit for this long-hold scenario, and the team already knows it well.
Either one is fine to pick, the final business outcome ends up the same.
Skip locking entirely and just rely on retry-after-failure to backstop consistency.
why: Redis 锁赢在性能与简单（Ticketmaster/Uber 场景）；但正确性优先 + 长持有 + 崩溃自动释放的需求下，ZK 的会话机制远比 Redis 的超时+心跳可靠。
why_en: Choose ZooKeeper locks when correctness trumps performance and locks are long-lived, since ephemeral nodes detect crashes more robustly than Redis timeouts.
whenOtherWins: 高频短锁场景（秒杀、抢票）Redis 性能更占优，Ticketmaster、Uber 都选了它。
tradeoff: ZooKeeper 锁的强一致 + 会话式崩溃检测 vs Redis 锁的高吞吐 + 手动超时管理

rows: 会话超时自动删除节点

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 锁：常用 SET key value NX EX ttl 实现，靠 TTL 超时兜底释放。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis lock is typically built with SET NX EX and relies on a TTL timeout as its safety net for release.

termDefinitions.meaning: quorum（多数派）：ZooKeeper 写操作需要 ensemble 过半服务器确认后才算成功。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A quorum is the majority of ensemble servers whose acknowledgment a ZooKeeper write needs before it succeeds.

optionExplanations: 对：正确性优先、锁可能持有数小时、崩溃要可靠检测——ZK 的会话+临时节点机制比 Redis 的超时管理更适合这种要求。
Redis 锁吞吐更高没错，但长时间持锁得把 TTL 设得远超预期时长，否则锁会提前失效，反而放进并发写。
两个方案在这个场景绝不等价：金融交易一旦并发写入就是资金错误，不能『随便选』。
不加锁靠失败重试根本替代不了互斥，并发交易可能直接导致重复扣款或超卖。
optionExplanations_en: Right: correctness first, hours-long holds, and reliable crash detection — ZooKeeper's session-based ephemeral nodes fit this better than Redis's timeout management.
Redis locks do give higher throughput, but a long hold means setting the TTL far past the expected duration, or the lock lapses early and lets in concurrent writes.
These two are never equivalent here — in finance a concurrent write means real monetary error, not something to leave to chance.
Skipping the lock and relying on retry-after-failure cannot substitute for mutual exclusion — concurrent transactions can double-charge or overspend funds.

scenario: ZK 自己也是一组多台机器：它的 leader 宕机时，必须先让自己内部对状态达成一致。
scenario_en: ZooKeeper is itself a cluster of machines, so when its own leader dies it must first get its members to agree on state.
q: ZooKeeper 内部靠什么协议达成共识？
q_en: Which protocol does ZooKeeper use internally for consensus?
options: Raft 协议，据说和 etcd 内部所使用的共识协议完全是同一套实现，只是换了个名字而已，没什么本质区别
ZAB（ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast）：让全体服务器在故障下仍对系统状态达成一致
Gossip 协议，节点之间随机两两交换状态信息、逐步扩散全局视图
关系型数据库里常见的两阶段锁协议，专门用来处理并发事务控制
options_en: Raft, supposedly the exact same implementation of the consensus protocol that etcd uses internally, just under a different name with no real difference.
ZAB, ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast, which lets all servers agree on system state despite failures.
Gossip, where nodes randomly exchange state with each other in pairs to gradually spread a global view.
Two-phase locking, the classic relational-database protocol for concurrent transaction control.
why: 有趣的反讽：ZK 帮别人解决协调问题，自己得先解决自己的——答案就是 ZAB 协议。
why_en: ZooKeeper runs the ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast protocol so all its servers agree on system state despite failures.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZAB：ZooKeeper 内部使用的共识协议，负责 leader 选举与写操作的原子广播。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZAB, ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast, is the consensus protocol ZooKeeper's own servers use for leader election and atomic write propagation.

termDefinitions.meaning: Raft：一种被广泛使用的分布式共识协议，etcd 等系统基于它实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Raft is a widely used distributed consensus protocol that systems like etcd are built on.

termDefinitions.meaning: Gossip 协议：节点间随机两两交换状态、逐步扩散信息的去中心化通信方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Gossip protocols spread state by having nodes randomly exchange information with each other in a decentralized way.

optionExplanations: ZAB 和 etcd 用的 Raft 是两套不同的实现，只是解决同类共识问题，不能划等号。
对：ZAB（ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast）让全体服务器在故障下仍对系统状态达成一致，是 ZK 自研的共识协议。
Gossip 靠节点间随机两两交换逐步扩散信息，ZK 用的是有 leader 的原子广播，不是去中心化的 gossip。
两阶段锁是关系数据库处理并发事务的机制，和跨服务器达成共识是完全不同的问题。
optionExplanations_en: ZAB and the Raft that etcd uses are two separate implementations solving the same class of problem — they are not the same protocol.
Right: ZAB, ZooKeeper Atomic Broadcast, lets all the servers agree on system state despite failures — it is ZooKeeper's own consensus protocol.
Gossip spreads information by random pairwise exchange; ZooKeeper instead uses leader-based atomic broadcast, not decentralized gossip.
Two-phase locking is a relational database's mechanism for concurrent transactions, a completely different problem from cross-server consensus.

scenario: 5 台 ZK 的 leader 宕机，集群恢复服务前必须保证已确认的写不丢、顺序不乱。
scenario_en: The leader of a five-node ZooKeeper ensemble dies, and before serving again the cluster must guarantee no acknowledged write is lost or reordered.
q: ZAB 协议的两个主要阶段是？
q_en: What are the two main phases of the ZAB protocol?
options: 大数据批处理里常见的映射（Map）和归约（Reduce）这两个阶段，跟服务器之间怎么达成共识完全无关
存储引擎设计里常见的压缩和解压这两个流程阶段
先选出 leader 协调者，再由它做原子广播：写请求经 leader 广播，多数派确认才算成功
网络传输协议里常见的加密和解密这两个流程阶段
options_en: The map and reduce phases common in big-data batch processing, which have nothing to do with how servers reach consensus.
Compress and decompress, the two phases common in storage engine design.
First elect a leader coordinator, then it does atomic broadcast: writes go through the leader and commit once a majority confirms.
Encrypt and decrypt, the two phases common in network transport protocols.
why: 先选主，再由主广播所有写并等 quorum 确认——两阶段合起来保证故障下的一致视图。
why_en: ZAB has leader election followed by atomic broadcast, where writes go through the leader and commit once a majority persists them.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Leader election"] --> B["Discovery"]
  B --> C["Sync"]
  C --> D["Broadcast writes"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 原子广播：leader 把一条写操作发给所有 follower，且保证要么大家都按同一顺序应用，要么不生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Atomic broadcast is the leader sending a write to all followers with the guarantee that everyone applies it in the same order, or not at all.

optionExplanations: Map/Reduce 是大数据批处理的阶段划分，和 ZK 内部达成共识的流程完全不是一回事。
压缩/解压是存储引擎节省空间的手段，跟服务器之间怎么对状态达成一致没有关系。
对：先选出 leader，再由它做原子广播——写请求经 leader 广播、多数派确认才算成功，这两步合起来才能在出故障时仍让所有服务器看到同一份状态。
加密/解密解决的是传输安全问题，不是 ZK 内部达成共识要走的流程。
optionExplanations_en: Map/Reduce is a big-data batch-processing split; it is nothing like how ZK internally reaches consensus.
Compress and decompress are storage-engine space-saving tricks, unrelated to how servers agree on state.
Right: first elect a leader, then it does atomic broadcast — writes go through the leader and commit once a majority confirms, together keeping a consistent view under failures.
Encrypt and decrypt address transport security, not the process ZooKeeper's own servers use to reach consensus.

scenario: ZK 内部换主时必须防止已提交的写丢失；应用层选举配方只需要一个公平的排队顺序。
scenario_en: ZooKeeper's internal leader change must not lose committed writes, while the application-level election recipe only needs a fair queue order.
q: ZK 内部的 leader 选举标准，与应用层「最小顺序节点当 leader」的配方有什么有趣的差别？
q_en: How does ZooKeeper's internal leader election differ from the application recipe?
options: 两者的判断标准其实完全一样，内部选举和应用层配方走的都是序号最小的那个胜出，彼此没有任何差别可言
内部选举优先「事务历史最新」的服务器，历史相同时选 ID 最高的——方向恰好与应用层「最小序号获胜」相反
内部选举其实是按服务器主机名做字典序排序，直接取排在最前面的那一台当 leader，跟它数据新不新无关
内部选举的结果其实完全由运维人员手工写进配置文件里去指定
options_en: Both use the exact same rule internally and at the application layer: the lowest sequence number wins, with no difference between them at all.
Internally the server with the most up-to-date transaction history wins, ties broken by highest ID, the opposite of the application-layer rule.
Internal election just sorts servers by hostname lexicographically and picks the first one as leader, regardless of how up-to-date its data is.
The internal election result is actually entirely hand-written by an operator into a config file.
why: 内部要的是「数据最全的节点当 leader」（防丢更新），平局取最高 ID；应用层配方取最小序号——内部机制与其上构建的模式可以完全不同。
why_en: Internally ZooKeeper elects the server with the most up-to-date transaction history, preferring the highest ID on ties, the opposite of the lowest-sequence application recipe.
tradeoff: 内部选举「数据最全者优先」（防丢写）vs 应用层配方「最小序号优先」（排队公平）
optionExplanations: 内部选举和应用层配方的方向其实相反，不是同一套规则，内部要的是数据最全的节点。
对：内部选举优先『事务历史最新』的服务器，平局取最高 ID，方向正好和应用层『最小序号获胜』相反——防止丢失已确认的更新。
内部选举不是按主机名字典序，那样选不出数据最完整的节点，无法保证不丢已确认的更新。
内部选举是自动运行的算法，不是靠运维手工写进配置文件指定的。
optionExplanations_en: Internal election and the application recipe actually point opposite directions, not the same rule — internally it is about who has the most complete data.

Right: internally the server with the most up-to-date transaction history wins, ties broken by the highest ID — the opposite of the application layer's 'lowest sequence wins', to avoid losing confirmed updates.
Internal election is not by hostname order — that would fail to pick the most complete node and could lose acknowledged updates.
Internal election runs as an automatic algorithm, not something an operator hand-writes into a config file.

scenario: 设计评审要拍板：换 etcd（Raft）还是留在 ZK（ZAB），共识保证上是否有本质差别。
scenario_en: A design review has to settle it: moving to etcd on Raft versus staying on ZooKeeper with ZAB — is there any real difference in consensus guarantees?
q: ZAB 与 Paxos / Raft 的关系是？
q_en: How are ZAB, Paxos, and Raft related?
options: 三者的目标和实现完全不相关，只是名字看起来像
ZAB 只是对 Raft 协议做了一层简单封装
ZAB 的功能已经被 Paxos 完全取代，现在的生产系统里已经没人再用它了
同类目标：都是分布式共识协议；ZAB 早于 Raft，实现细节不同但高层目标一致
options_en: The three are unrelated in goal and implementation; they just sound similar.
ZAB is just a thin wrapper around the Raft protocol.
ZAB has been completely superseded by Paxos, and no production system uses it anymore today.
Same family: all are distributed consensus protocols; ZAB predates Raft and differs in details but shares the high-level goal.
why: ZAB、Paxos、Raft 都解决「多副本对状态达成一致」；面试里可以把 ZAB 类比成 ZK 自家的共识协议。
why_en: ZAB predates Raft and differs in implementation, but like Paxos and Raft it achieves distributed consensus.

termDefinitions.meaning: Paxos：最早提出的分布式共识协议之一，理论严谨但实现较复杂。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Paxos is one of the earliest distributed consensus protocols, theoretically rigorous but notoriously hard to implement.

optionExplanations: 三者名字像不是巧合——它们的目标都是分布式共识，实现细节不同但要解决的问题是一类。
ZAB 不是套壳 Raft，它是 ZooKeeper 自研、早于 Raft 出现的独立协议。
ZAB 没有被 Paxos 取代，它至今仍在 ZooKeeper 内部实际运行。
对：三者本质上是同一类协议——都要解决分布式共识；ZAB 出现得比 Raft 早，实现细节不同但目标一致。
optionExplanations_en: The similar names are not a coincidence — all three target distributed consensus, just with different implementation details.
ZAB is not a thin wrapper around Raft — it is ZooKeeper's own protocol, predating Raft.
ZAB was not superseded by Paxos — it still runs inside ZooKeeper today.
Right: ZAB, Paxos, and Raft are all distributed consensus protocols aiming at the same goal; ZAB predates Raft and differs in details but shares the high-level target.

q: 补全 ZooKeeper 的一致性保证：
q_en: Fill in ZooKeeper's consistency guarantees.
text: 五大保证：{{顺序一致性}}（同一客户端的更新按发送顺序生效）、{{原子性}}（更新要么全成要么全败）、{{单一系统映像}}（连哪台服务器看到的视图一致）、{{持久性}}（确认过的更新不会丢）、及时性（客户端视图在有界时间内更新）。
why: 这五条是 ZK 可以被信任为「协调真相源」的原因；实现上全靠写走 leader 的全序 + quorum 持久化。
why_en: ZooKeeper guarantees sequential consistency, atomicity, a single system image, durability, and timeliness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序一致性：同一客户端发出的多个更新，所有服务器都按发送顺序应用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential consistency means updates from one client are applied by every server in the order that client sent them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单一系统映像：无论客户端连到 ensemble 里哪台服务器，同步后看到的数据视图都一样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A single system image means a client sees the same data view regardless of which ensemble server it connects to, once synced.

scenario: 聊天服务器刚写完 Bob 的新路由，立刻从另一台 follower 读回来校验，不能读到旧值。
scenario_en: A chat server has just written Bob's new routing and immediately reads it back from a different follower to verify — a stale value is unacceptable.
q: 从 follower 读数据可能读到旧值。需要最强一致的读时怎么办？
q_en: Follower reads can be stale. What should you do when you need the strongest read consistency?
options: 把所有读请求都强制改发给 leader 一台机器处理，其它节点彻底闲置不用
读前先调用 sync 操作，确保该服务器已与 leader 同步再读
同一份数据读三次，取出现次数最多的那个结果
这个问题无解，只能接受可能读到旧数据
options_en: Force every read request to go only to the leader, leaving every other node completely idle.
Call sync before reading, ensuring the server has caught up with the leader first.
Read the same value three times and take the majority result.
There is no fix — you just accept that reads may be stale.
why: follower 平时不为每次读询问 leader，所以可能滞后；sync 强制先追平再读，换来最新数据。
why_en: Follower reads can be stale, so clients call sync before reading when they need the most up-to-date view.

termDefinitions.meaning: sync：一个强制 follower 先追平 leader 最新状态、再返回读结果的操作，用于换取最强一致读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: sync is an operation that forces a follower to catch up with the leader's latest state before serving a read, trading latency for the strongest consistency.

optionExplanations: 把所有读都逼去 leader 一台机器，等于放弃了『任意节点都能读』这个可扩展性优势。
对：读前先调用 sync，强制该服务器先追平 leader 最新状态再读，用一次额外往返换来最强一致。
读三次取多数在 ZK 里没有意义——多个副本本就在同步收敛，比的不是投票而是谁追上了 leader。
这个问题其实有解，sync 操作正是为了在需要时换取最新数据。
optionExplanations_en: Forcing all reads onto the leader alone throws away the scalability benefit of letting any node serve reads.
Right: calling sync before reading forces that server to catch up with the leader's latest state first, trading one extra round trip for the strongest consistency.
Reading three times and taking a majority does not make sense here — replicas are converging by sync, not by a voting scheme.
This actually does have a fix — the sync operation exists precisely to trade latency for freshness when you need it.

scenario: 选型时要判断 ZooKeeper 是否适合当前系统。
scenario_en: During technology selection you need to judge whether ZooKeeper fits.
q: ZooKeeper 官方文档描述它在哪种读写比例的负载下表现最好？
q_en: According to the official ZooKeeper documentation, at what read/write ratio does it perform best?
options: 写多读少：大部分请求是更新配置或路由信息
读写各占一半
读主导，约 10:1 的读写比
写主导，约 1:10 的读写比
options_en: Write-heavy: most requests update config or routing
Roughly even split between reads and writes
Read-dominant, around 10:1 reads to writes
Write-dominant, around 1:10 reads to writes
why: 读由客户端连接的那台服务器从本地内存直接返回（不走 quorum，可能略旧，需要时用 sync），写必须经 leader 走 ZAB 多数派确认。官方文档称它在读主导、约 10:1 的负载下表现最好；所以服务发现这类读多写少场景适合，写多的日志采集不适合。
why_en: Reads are served from the local in-memory replica of whichever server the client is connected to (no quorum, possibly slightly stale; use sync when needed), while writes go through the leader and ZAB majority acknowledgment. The official docs say it performs best in read-dominant workloads around 10:1, so read-heavy service discovery fits and write-heavy log collection does not.
optionExplanations: 写多读少形容的是日志采集这类场景，和 ZK 架构「读走本地内存、写要走 leader+quorum」的设计取向正相反。
读写各半会让「写必须经 leader」这个昂贵路径占比过高，不是官方描述的最佳负载。
对：读由连接的服务器从本地内存直接返回，写必须过 leader 走多数派确认；官方文档称读主导、约 10:1 时表现最好。
错：写主导会让 leader 与 quorum 写路径成为瓶颈，和官方描述的读主导最佳负载正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Write-heavy describes something like log collection, the opposite of ZooKeeper's design: reads from local memory, writes through leader plus quorum.
An even split still pushes a lot of traffic through the expensive leader-plus-quorum write path; it is not the best workload per the docs.
Right: reads are served from the connected server's local memory while writes go through the leader with majority acknowledgment; the docs say it performs best read-dominant, around 10:1.
Wrong: a write-dominant load makes the leader and quorum write path the bottleneck, the opposite of the read-dominant sweet spot in the docs.

scenario: 聊天服务器用临时节点登记在线状态，进程崩溃后这条登记必须自动消失，不能留残影。
scenario_en: Chat servers register liveness with ephemeral nodes, and the entry has to disappear on its own when the process crashes — no ghost entries.
q: ZooKeeper 会话（session）机制的要点是？
q_en: What are the key points of ZooKeeper sessions?
options: 会话一旦建立成功就永不过期，客户端可以一直保持连接下去
会话本质上就是一条 TCP 连接，这条连接一断会话就立刻失效
会话完全由 ensemble 的 leader 手动维护，客户端不参与任何交互，也不用发心跳，全靠服务端单方面兜底判断客户端还活着
客户端建立带超时（典型 10-30 秒）的会话，靠心跳维持；断连后可换服务器恢复会话，过期则清理其临时节点和 watch
options_en: Once established, a session never expires and the client can stay connected forever.
A session is essentially just one TCP connection, and it dies the instant that connection drops.
