The session is maintained entirely by the ensemble's leader; the client takes part in nothing, sends no heartbeats, and the server decides single-handedly whether the client is alive.
Clients hold a heartbeat-maintained session with a typical 10-30 second timeout; expiry cleans up its ephemeral nodes and watches.
why: 会话是临时节点和故障检测的地基：心跳没到、超时到期，就视为客户端死亡并自动清理它的痕迹。
why_en: Clients hold heartbeat-maintained sessions with a ten-to-thirty-second timeout, and expiry deletes their ephemeral nodes and watches.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Client session"] --> B["Heartbeat"]
  B --> C{"Timeout?"}
  C -->|"no"| A
  C -->|"yes"| D["Delete ephemeral nodes"]

termDefinitions.meaning: session（会话）：客户端与 ZooKeeper 之间靠心跳维持的逻辑连接，可以跨越多次 TCP 重连而存续。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A session is a heartbeat-maintained logical connection between client and ZooKeeper that can survive multiple TCP reconnects.

termDefinitions.meaning: TCP：一种保证有序、可靠传输的底层网络协议；ZooKeeper 会话建立在 TCP 连接之上，但会话本身能跨越重连存续。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is the underlying reliable, ordered transport protocol; a ZooKeeper session sits on top of a TCP connection but can outlive a single reconnect.

optionExplanations: 会话不过期就没法在崩溃时清理临时节点，故障检测这套机制直接失效。
把会话等同于一条 TCP 连接会把短暂网络抖动误判成客户端死亡，触发不必要的切换。
会话机制本就需要客户端配合发心跳，靠 leader 单方面维护无法及时发现客户端已经死掉。
对：客户端建立带超时（典型 10-30 秒）的会话靠心跳维持，断连可换服务器恢复，过期才清理临时节点和 watch。
optionExplanations_en: If sessions never expired, there would be no way to clean up ephemeral nodes on a crash — failure detection would just stop working.
Equating a session with one TCP connection would misread a brief network blip as client death and trigger an unnecessary failover.
The session mechanism needs the client to send heartbeats; leader-only upkeep cannot promptly detect that a client has died.
Right: clients hold a heartbeat-maintained session with a typical 10-30 second timeout, can reconnect to a different server before it expires, and only expiry cleans up ephemeral nodes and watches.

scenario: 聊天集群跨机房部署，链路偶发 5 秒抖动，但真宕机要在半分钟内被发现。
scenario_en: The chat cluster spans datacenters with occasional five-second network stalls, yet a genuine crash must be detected within half a minute.
q: 会话超时（session timeout）设置的两难是？
q_en: What tradeoff does the ZooKeeper session timeout setting create?
options: 设太短：临时网络抖动就误判死亡引发不必要的失效/切换；设太长：真故障要等很久才被发现
无论把这个值设得再长或者再短，实际观察到的效果完全一样
会话超时值只会小幅影响服务器进程的内存占用大小
会话超时值只会影响 ZooKeeper 每天写出的日志文件总量，跟故障检测速度没关系
options_en: Too short causes false failovers on network blips; too long delays detecting real failures.
Setting the value longer or shorter produces exactly the same observed effect either way.
The timeout value only has a minor effect on how much memory the server process uses.
The timeout value only affects how much log file volume ZooKeeper writes out per day, unrelated to failure-detection speed.
why: 这是所有故障检测的通用权衡：灵敏 vs 稳定。10-30 秒的典型值就是在两者间折中。
why_en: A short session timeout causes false failovers on network blips, while a long one delays detecting real failures.
optionExplanations: 对：设太短，网络一抖动就被误判成死亡触发不必要的切换；设太长，真出故障也要等很久才被发现。
超时值长短对实际表现影响很大，不是『设成什么都一样』。
超时值主要影响的是故障检测的灵敏度，对内存占用的影响是次要甚至可以忽略的。
超时值决定的是判断死亡的快慢，不是日志文件写出的多少。
optionExplanations_en: Right: too short and a network blip gets misread as death, triggering an unneeded failover; too long and a real failure takes ages to be caught.
The timeout value has a real effect on behavior — it is not the case that any setting looks the same.
The timeout value mainly affects how quickly failures are detected, not how much memory the process uses — that impact is minor at best.
The timeout value decides how fast death gets detected, not how much log volume gets written.

scenario: ZK 已经回复客户端「Bob 的路由写成功」，就在这一刻整个 ensemble 断电重启。
scenario_en: ZooKeeper has already told the client that Bob's routing write succeeded, and at that exact moment the whole ensemble loses power and reboots.
q: ZooKeeper 靠什么保证「确认过的更新永不丢失」？
q_en: How does ZooKeeper make sure acknowledged updates are not lost?
options: 把每一次写操作产生的数据都顺手额外同步一份到远端云对象存储服务里去，图个双重保险，防止本地磁盘一坏就再也找不回来
每个状态变更先写持久化的事务日志（WAL，须先落盘再响应）；周期性做内存数据库快照，重启时加载快照+重放日志恢复
只要在三台服务器各自的内存里都稳定保留一份副本数据就已经足够可靠
让每一个连接进来的客户端都在本地缓存一份完整数据作为额外的备份手段
options_en: On every write, also sync a copy off to a remote cloud object store as double insurance, so a local disk failure never loses the data for good.
Each change is first written to a persistent write-ahead transaction log, then periodic snapshots speed up recovery by replaying the log.
Keeping one steady in-memory replica on each of three servers is already reliable enough.
Every connected client also keeps a full local cache of the data as an extra backup measure.
why: WAL + 快照是经典持久化组合：日志保证不丢，快照加速恢复。官方强调事务日志是 ZK 最性能攸关的部分，建议独立日志盘。
why_en: Every change is synced to a write-ahead transaction log before responding, and periodic snapshots speed up recovery on restart.

termDefinitions.meaning: WAL（预写日志）：先把变更写进持久化日志、确认落盘后才响应客户端的技术，保证崩溃不丢已确认的更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A write-ahead log records a change durably before responding to the client, guaranteeing acknowledged updates survive a crash.

termDefinitions.meaning: 快照：内存数据库某一时刻的完整落盘副本，重启时先加载快照再重放之后的日志，加速恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A snapshot is a point-in-time on-disk copy of the in-memory database; restart loads it first and then replays the log for faster recovery.

optionExplanations: 额外同步到云对象存储不是 ZK 保证不丢更新的机制，它靠的是自己先落盘的事务日志。
对：每个变更先写持久化的事务日志（须先落盘再响应），再周期性做快照，重启时加载快照+重放日志恢复。
只在内存里保留副本，进程一崩就全丢，光靠三台内存副本没有落盘保证，靠不住。
客户端本地缓存是给读用的加速手段，不是服务端保证已确认更新不丢的机制。
optionExplanations_en: Syncing off to cloud object storage is not how ZK guarantees no lost updates; it relies on its own on-disk transaction log.
Right: each change is written to a persistent transaction log first, must hit disk before responding, and periodic snapshots let restart load the snapshot then replay the log.
Keeping replicas only in memory means a crash loses everything — three in-memory copies with nothing on disk is not durable.
A client-side local cache speeds up reads — it is not the server-side mechanism that guarantees acknowledged updates survive.

scenario: ZK 节点的 JVM 堆超过了物理内存，操作系统开始把部分数据页换出到磁盘。
scenario_en: A ZooKeeper node's JVM heap grows past physical memory and the operating system starts swapping data pages out to disk.
q: 为什么内存交换（swapping）对 ZooKeeper 性能是灾难性的？
q_en: Why is swapping disastrous for ZooKeeper performance?
options: swap 会直接损坏磁盘上已经持久化的事务日志数据
swap 发生时 ZooKeeper 会强制断开所有已连接的客户端，逼大家重新连接
ZK 的所有操作是全序执行的：一个请求因 swap 卡在磁盘，后面排队的所有请求都被拖住
swap 只会让 watch 通知机制暂时失效几秒钟，等换页结束后一切自动恢复正常，对整体影响其实很有限
options_en: Swapping directly corrupts the transaction log already persisted on disk.
Swapping forces ZooKeeper to disconnect every connected client immediately, forcing everyone to reconnect.
All operations execute in total order: one request stuck on disk due to swap delays every request queued behind it.
Swapping only makes the watch-notification mechanism drop out for a few seconds; once paging finishes everything recovers on its own, so the impact is quite limited.
why: 全序流水线意味着「一人慢全队慢」：内存读约 100ns，换页回磁盘约 10ms ≈ 慢 10 万倍。堆要留足，让数据集全驻内存。
why_en: ZooKeeper executes requests in total order, so one request paging in from disk — about 10ms versus 100ns from memory — stalls everything queued behind it.
optionExplanations: swap 是内存和磁盘之间的换页，不会直接损坏已经落盘的事务日志内容。
swap 发生时 ZooKeeper 不会主动断开全部客户端，它只是处理变慢了。
对：ZK 所有操作全序执行，一个请求因 swap 卡在磁盘 I/O 上，后面排队的全部请求都被一起拖住。
swap 拖慢的是整条全序流水线，后果远不止『通知失效几秒』，而是所有排队请求一起被拖死。
optionExplanations_en: Swapping is paging between memory and disk — it does not directly corrupt a transaction log already persisted.
Swapping does not make ZooKeeper actively disconnect every client — it just makes everything slower.
Right: all operations execute in total order, so one request stuck on swap-induced disk I/O drags down every request queued behind it.
Swapping slows the entire total-order pipeline; the impact is far beyond a few seconds of lost notifications — every queued request stalls together.

scenario: 5 台 ZK 被网络分区切成 2+2+1 三组，任何一组都凑不齐 3 票的多数派。
scenario_en: A network partition splits a five-node ensemble into groups of two, two, and one, so no group can reach the three-vote majority.
q: 网络分区导致任何一组服务器都凑不齐多数派时，ZooKeeper 会怎样？
q_en: What does ZooKeeper do when no network partition can form a majority?
options: 分区两边的服务器各自继续独立处理写请求，等分区恢复后再合并数据，尽量减少停机时间
自动在云上现拉起几台新的服务器节点来补足所需的多数派
由系统随机挑其中一边的服务器组，继续处理这一边的写请求
停止处理写请求直到分区恢复——宁可不可用也要避免 split-brain（脑裂）
options_en: Both sides of the partition keep processing writes independently and merge the data after it heals, to minimize downtime.
It automatically spins up a few new servers in the cloud to restore a majority.
The system randomly picks one side of the partition to keep processing its writes.
It stops processing writes until the partition heals, choosing unavailability over split-brain.
why: 没有多数派就不写，防止系统两半各持一套「真相」；这是 CP 系统的典型选择。
why_en: Without a majority ZooKeeper refuses writes until the partition heals, preventing split-brain disagreement.

termDefinitions.meaning: split-brain（脑裂）：网络分区后系统两半各自独立接受写入，产生两份互相矛盾的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Split-brain is when a network partition lets both halves of a system independently accept writes, producing two conflicting copies of the data.

termDefinitions.meaning: CP 系统：在 CAP 权衡中优先保证一致性和分区容忍、宁可牺牲可用性的系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CP system is one that, in the CAP tradeoff, prioritizes consistency and partition tolerance even at the cost of availability.

optionExplanations: 两边都继续处理写请求正是脑裂本身，分区恢复后两份数据早就互相矛盾，合并不回去。
网络分区期间 ZooKeeper 不会自动在云上拉起新机器来凑多数派，这需要人工介入。
随机选一边继续写同样会制造出脑裂，被抛弃那边的写入还是丢了。
对：凑不齐多数派就停止处理写请求，直到分区恢复——宁可不可用也不让两边各自持有不同的『真相』。
optionExplanations_en: Both sides continuing to write is split-brain itself — once the partition heals, the two histories have already diverged and cannot simply merge back.
ZooKeeper does not auto-provision new cloud servers during a partition to restore a majority — that needs human intervention.
Randomly picking one side to keep writing still produces split-brain — the abandoned side's writes are still lost.
Right: without a majority it stops processing writes until the partition heals, choosing unavailability over letting the two sides hold different versions of the truth.

q: 把「聊天服务器崩溃后 ZooKeeper 的自动处理」排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put ZooKeeper's automatic handling of a crashed chat server in the right order.
steps: 其它 watch 这些节点的服务器收到通知，更新路由表、把用户标记下线
它创建的所有临时节点被自动删除（服务器注册节点 + 名下用户节点）
Server 2 的 ZK 会话超时（典型 10-30 秒后）
why: 崩溃 → 会话超时 → 临时节点消失 → watcher 收通知并响应。全程无需人工干预——这是 ZK 最强大的特性之一。
why_en: After a crash the session times out, its ephemeral nodes are deleted, and watching servers get notified and update their routing automatically.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    C["Server 2 崩溃"] --> T["会话超时"]
    T --> D["临时节点自动删除"]
    D --> N["watcher 收到通知\n更新路由/标记下线"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 会话超时：客户端超过约定时间没有发送心跳，ZooKeeper 判定其会话失效并清理其临时节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session timeout is when a client misses heartbeats for the agreed window, so ZooKeeper marks its session expired and cleans up its ephemeral nodes.

scenario: 团队在决定要不要继续保留 ZK 运维能力，先得弄清哪些在跑的系统仍硬依赖它。
scenario_en: Your team is deciding whether to keep ZooKeeper operations skills on staff, which starts with knowing which running systems still hard-depend on it.
q: 今天哪些系统仍然依赖 ZooKeeper？
q_en: Which systems still depend on ZooKeeper today?
options: Apache 生态核心组件：HBase、Hadoop、Storm、Pulsar 等；ClickHouse 复制协调也依赖它
有人误以为 Kubernetes 的核心调度组件是直接构建在 ZooKeeper 协调服务之上的，其实用的是自研的 etcd
几乎所有主流的云托管数据库和缓存产品线，据说如今都还依赖它来做协调
有人认为已经完全没有任何生产系统还在实际使用 ZooKeeper 了
options_en: Core Apache-ecosystem components: HBase, Hadoop, Storm, Pulsar and more; ClickHouse also relies on it for replication coordination.
Some mistakenly believe Kubernetes' core scheduler is built directly on top of the ZooKeeper coordination service, when it actually uses its own etcd.
Some claim nearly every mainstream cloud-managed database and cache product line today still depends on it.
Some believe there is no production system left anywhere that actually still uses ZooKeeper.
why: ZK 在 Apache 生态依然是台柱；ClickHouse 的复制部署也要求它。它老了，但没退休。
why_en: ZooKeeper remains central to HBase, Hadoop, SolrCloud, Storm, NiFi, and Pulsar, and ClickHouse requires it for replication coordination.
optionExplanations: 对：HBase、Hadoop、Storm、Pulsar 这些 Apache 生态核心组件仍在用它，ClickHouse 做副本协调时同样离不开它。
Kubernetes 的调度核心是自研的 etcd 存储，不是构建在 ZooKeeper 之上，这是常见的误解。
主流云托管数据库和缓存产品线大多不依赖 ZooKeeper，这个说法把它的覆盖范围夸大了。
说没有生产系统还在用它并不准确，Apache 生态和 ClickHouse 复制仍然实实在在依赖它。
optionExplanations_en: Right: core Apache-ecosystem components like HBase, Hadoop, Storm, and Pulsar still use it, and ClickHouse relies on it for replication coordination too.
Kubernetes' scheduling core is built on its own etcd store, not on top of ZooKeeper — a common misconception.
Most mainstream cloud-managed databases and caches do not actually depend on ZooKeeper — that overstates its reach.
Claiming no production system uses it anymore is inaccurate — the Apache ecosystem and ClickHouse replication genuinely still depend on it.

scenario: Kafka 用 KRaft 内置 Raft 取代了外部 ZK，团队要判断新系统还该不该外挂协调服务。
scenario_en: Kafka replaced its external ZooKeeper with built-in Raft via KRaft, and your team must decide whether a new system should still bolt on a coordination service.
q: Kafka 摆脱 ZooKeeper 的举动（KRaft）说明了什么趋势？
q_en: What trend does Kafka's move away from ZooKeeper with KRaft show?
options: 说明共识协议这类机制在分布式系统里已经变得不再重要
说明所有系统今后都应该反过来外挂一个独立的 ZooKeeper 集群才对，而不是自己内置共识算法，回到集中协调那条老路上去
转向「自带内置共识协议的自包含系统」：KRaft 消除了外部协调服务带来的运维复杂度、扩展瓶颈和故障点
说明 Kafka 已经彻底放弃了分布式架构，改回单机部署模式
options_en: It shows consensus mechanisms like this no longer matter in distributed systems.
It means every system should instead bolt on a separate ZooKeeper cluster rather than embed its own consensus, going back to the old centralized-coordination path.
A shift toward self-contained systems with built-in consensus: KRaft removes the ops complexity, scaling bottlenecks, and failure points of an external coordinator.
It shows Kafka has completely abandoned distributed architecture and gone back to single-node deployment.
why: 多年依赖后，Kafka 用内置 Raft 元数据模式替换 ZK——外部协调服务正在被内嵌共识取代，这是大势。
why_en: Kafka's move to KRaft reflects a broader trend toward self-contained systems with built-in consensus instead of external coordination services.

termDefinitions.meaning: KRaft：Kafka 内置的基于 Raft 的元数据管理模式，用来取代外部 ZooKeeper 依赖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KRaft is Kafka's built-in Raft-based metadata mode that replaces its former dependency on external ZooKeeper.

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka：分布式消息队列/事件流平台，曾长期用 ZooKeeper 管理集群元数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed messaging and event-streaming platform that long relied on ZooKeeper for cluster metadata.

optionExplanations: KRaft 恰恰是换成另一套共识协议（Raft）内置进来，说明共识机制依然核心，不是变得不重要。
现实方向正相反：Kafka 正在移除对外部 ZooKeeper 的依赖，不是反过来让所有系统都去外挂它。
对：转向『自带内置共识协议的自包含系统』，KRaft 消除了外部协调服务带来的运维复杂度、扩展瓶颈和故障点。
KRaft 之后 Kafka 仍是多 broker 分布式集群，只是元数据管理方式变了，不是退回单机部署。
optionExplanations_en: KRaft actually swaps in another consensus protocol, Raft, built-in — showing consensus is still core, not that it stopped mattering.
The real direction is the opposite: Kafka is removing its external ZooKeeper dependency, not pushing every system to bolt one on.
Right: it is a shift toward self-contained systems with built-in consensus — KRaft removes the ops complexity, scaling bottlenecks, and failure points of an external coordinator.
Post-KRaft Kafka is still a distributed multi-broker cluster; only metadata management changed, not a retreat to single-node deployment.

scenario: 要给一个跑在 Kubernetes 上的新服务选协调组件，团队只有 Go 和 HTTP/gRPC 栈经验。
scenario_en: You are choosing a coordination component for a new service on Kubernetes, and the team only has Go and HTTP/gRPC experience.
q: etcd 相对 ZooKeeper 的定位是？
q_en: How is etcd positioned relative to ZooKeeper?
options: 很多人误以为 etcd 只是把 ZooKeeper 原封不动地用 Java 语言重新实现了一遍而已，接口协议全照搬，只是改了个包名罢了
云原生世界的协调新贵：强一致分布式 KV，现代 HTTP/JSON 与 gRPC API，是 Kubernetes 的底座
很多人以为 etcd 只能拿来做服务发现，完全不支持用它存放配置数据
很多人误以为 etcd 本质是最终一致的存储系统，不提供任何强一致性保证
options_en: Many wrongly think etcd is just ZooKeeper reimplemented verbatim in Java, copying its interfaces and protocol, with only the package name changed.
The cloud-native coordinator: a strongly consistent distributed key-value store with modern HTTP/JSON and gRPC APIs, the base of Kubernetes.
Many believe etcd can only be used for service discovery and does not support storing configuration at all.
Many mistakenly believe etcd is fundamentally an eventually consistent store with no strong consistency guarantee.
why: etcd 与 ZK 解决同类问题（配置管理、服务发现），但 API 更现代、与云原生生态深度绑定。
why_en: Etcd offers strongly consistent key-value coordination with modern HTTP and gRPC APIs and powers Kubernetes.
tradeoff: etcd 的现代云原生 API + Kubernetes 深度集成 vs ZooKeeper 的 Apache 生态成熟度 + 更丰富的原生配方（选举/锁）

termDefinitions.meaning: etcd：基于 Raft 协议的强一致分布式键值存储，是 Kubernetes 的核心元数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: etcd is a strongly consistent distributed key-value store built on Raft that serves as Kubernetes' core metadata store.

termDefinitions.meaning: gRPC：Google 开源的高性能 RPC 框架，基于 HTTP/2 和 Protocol Buffers。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is Google's high-performance remote-procedure-call framework built on HTTP/2 and Protocol Buffers.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP/JSON：用标准 HTTP 请求携带 JSON 格式数据的接口风格，浏览器和多数语言都能直接用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP/JSON is an API style using standard HTTP requests with JSON payloads, directly usable from browsers and most languages.

optionExplanations: etcd 和 ZooKeeper 的协议、数据模型、API 完全不同，不是简单把 ZK 用别的语言重写一遍。
对：etcd 是云原生世界的协调新贵——强一致分布式 KV，现代 HTTP/JSON 与 gRPC API，是 Kubernetes 的底座。
etcd 的 KV 接口天然适合存配置，很多平台的配置中心底层就是它，不是『不支持』。
etcd 基于 Raft，和 ZAB 一样提供强一致写，不是最终一致存储。
optionExplanations_en: etcd's protocol, data model, and API differ entirely from ZooKeeper's — it is not ZK rewritten in another language.
Right: etcd is the cloud-native coordinator — a strongly consistent distributed key-value store with modern HTTP/JSON and gRPC APIs, powering Kubernetes.
etcd's key-value interface fits configuration naturally, and it backs many platforms' config centers — it does support this.
etcd is built on Raft and, like ZAB, gives strongly consistent writes — it is not an eventually consistent store.

scenario: 微服务集群要求实例上下线时自动重配负载均衡器和防火墙规则，还要带健康检查。
scenario_en: A microservice cluster needs load balancers and firewall rules reconfigured automatically as instances come and go, health checks included.
q: Consul 与 ZooKeeper 相比的特色是？
q_en: What is Consul's distinguishing feature compared with ZooKeeper?
options: Consul 只是把 ZooKeeper 用 Go 语言重新实现了一遍
Consul 的能力范围其实比 ZooKeeper 更窄，只提供分布式锁这一项功能，服务发现和 KV 存储一概做不了
Consul 不做健康检查，这方面反而不如 ZooKeeper
超出基础协调：服务发现 + 健康检查 + KV 存储，招牌是按服务变化自动重配负载均衡器和防火墙
options_en: Consul is just ZooKeeper reimplemented in Go with the same feature set.
Consul is actually narrower than ZooKeeper, offering only distributed locking and none of service discovery or KV storage.
Consul does not do health checking, which is actually a gap compared to ZooKeeper.
It goes beyond basic coordination: service discovery, health checking, and a KV store, with automatic load-balancer and firewall reconfiguration as its signature feature.
why: Consul 走「更全家桶」路线；云厂商方案（AWS Parameter Store、Azure App Configuration 等）则以托管省心取胜。
why_en: Consul goes beyond coordination with service discovery, health checks, and network automation that reconfigures load balancers as services change.
tradeoff: Consul 的服务网格全家桶（服务发现+健康检查+网络自动化）vs ZooKeeper 的专注协调原语（ZNode+watch）

rows: 发现+健康检查+网络自动化

termDefinitions.meaning: Consul：HashiCorp 出品的协调服务，除服务发现外还内置健康检查和网络自动化能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Consul is HashiCorp's coordination service that adds built-in health checking and network automation on top of service discovery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 健康检查：持续探测服务实例是否正常运行，异常时自动从可用列表摘除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A health check continuously probes whether a service instance is functioning and removes it from the available list when it is not.

optionExplanations: Consul 的一致性协议、数据模型和功能范围都和 ZooKeeper 不同，不是简单换个语言重写。
Consul 的能力范围其实比 ZooKeeper 更宽，服务发现、健康检查、KV 存储都有，不只是分布式锁。
健康检查恰恰是 Consul 的内置能力，说它『不如 ZooKeeper』方向反了。
对：Consul 超出基础协调，内置服务发现、健康检查、KV 存储，招牌是按服务变化自动重配负载均衡器和防火墙。
optionExplanations_en: Consul's consensus protocol, data model, and feature scope all differ from ZooKeeper's — it is not just a Go rewrite.
Consul is actually broader than ZooKeeper — service discovery, health checks, and KV storage — not just distributed locking.
Health checking is actually a built-in Consul capability — claiming it falls short of ZooKeeper here has it backwards.

Right: Consul goes beyond basic coordination with service discovery, health checking, and a KV store, with its signature move being automatic load-balancer and firewall reconfiguration as services change.

scenario: 百万聊天用户同时上线，客户端全都 watch 同一个 /chat-app/servers 节点。
scenario_en: A million chat users come online at once and every client watches the same /chat-app/servers node.
q: ZooKeeper 的「热点问题（hot spotting）」指什么？
q_en: What does ZooKeeper hot spotting mean?
options: 服务器 CPU 长期处于持续高负载运行状态，触发了系统的自动降频保护机制导致变慢，跟大量 watch 集中在同一节点无关
大量客户端 watch 同一个 ZNode（选举、锁的常态）时，通知流量可能压垮服务器——热门节点成为瓶颈
系统会自动把被频繁访问的热数据迁移到内存容量更大的机器上去
磁盘上的某个存储扇区因为被反复频繁写入而提前发生物理损坏
options_en: The server CPU sits under sustained high load and trips automatic down-clocking, unrelated to many watches piling onto one node.
When many clients watch the same znode, common in election or locks, notification traffic can overwhelm servers — popular nodes become bottlenecks.
The system automatically migrates frequently accessed hot data onto machines with larger memory capacity.
A specific storage sector wears out and fails early from being written to over and over.
why: 想象聊天例子里百万用户同时上线：同一节点的海量 watch 通知是规模化的天花板之一。
why_en: When many clients watch the same znode, notification traffic can overwhelm the servers and popular nodes become bottlenecks.

termDefinitions.meaning: hot spotting（热点问题）：大量请求或 watch 集中在同一个节点上，导致该节点及其所在服务器成为瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hot spotting is when a large volume of requests or watches concentrate on a single node, turning it and its server into a bottleneck.

optionExplanations: CPU 自动降频和这里问的『大量 watch 集中在同一节点』完全不是一回事，是找错了原因。
对：大量客户端 watch 同一个 ZNode（选举、锁的常态）时，通知流量会压垮服务器，热门节点自己变成瓶颈。
ZooKeeper 不会自动把热数据搬到内存更大的机器上，它没有这种自动数据迁移能力。
磁盘扇区物理损坏是硬件层面的问题，和这里说的『大量客户端盯着同一节点』完全不相关。
optionExplanations_en: CPU auto down-clocking is nothing like the many-watches-on-one-node issue being asked about — it points at the wrong cause.
Right: when many clients watch the same znode, common during elections or locks, the notification traffic can overwhelm servers and the popular node becomes the bottleneck itself.
ZooKeeper does not automatically migrate hot data to bigger-memory machines — it has no such auto-migration capability.
Physical disk-sector wear is a hardware-layer issue, unrelated to lots of clients watching the same node.

scenario: 要把 ZK 用在写入密集、数据集达数十 GB 的场景前，先评估它的天花板在哪里。
scenario_en: Before putting ZooKeeper behind a write-heavy workload with a dataset in the tens of gigabytes, you need to know where its ceilings are.
q: ZooKeeper 的主要局限有哪些？（多选）
q_en: What are ZooKeeper's main limitations? (Select all that apply.)
options: 写昂贵：必须经 leader 传播到多数派
内存存储模型限制容量：ZNode 要 <1MB、数据集须装进内存
运维复杂：JVM 参数、磁盘布局、超时与连接监控——「用起来简单，运维起来复杂」
不支持 watch 通知，只能靠轮询感知变化
options_en: Writes are expensive: they must propagate through the leader to a majority.
Capacity is memory-bound: znodes must stay under one megabyte and the dataset must fit in memory.
Operationally complex: JVM tuning, disk layout, timeout and connection monitoring — simple to use, complex to operate.
It does not support watch notifications, so changes can only be detected by polling.
why: 存大量数据、扛超高写入、或想最小化运维时，都该考虑替代方案；watch 恰恰是它的招牌能力，不是局限。
why_en: ZooKeeper writes are expensive through leader and quorum, capacity is memory-bound with small znodes, and it is simple to use but complex to operate.

termDefinitions.meaning: JVM：运行 Java 程序的虚拟机；ZooKeeper 用 Java 实现，堆大小等 JVM 参数需要仔细调优。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The JVM is the runtime that executes Java programs; ZooKeeper is written in Java, so JVM settings like heap size need careful tuning.

optionExplanations: 写昂贵是真实限制：每次写都要经 leader 广播并等多数派确认，高频写入场景会先撑不住。
内存存储模型限制容量：单个 ZNode 要 <1MB，数据集必须整体能装进内存，大数据量不该塞进去。
运维复杂是真实痛点：JVM 堆调优、独立日志盘、超时和连接监控——用起来简单，运维起来处处是细节。
这个选项说反了——推送通知正是它的招牌能力，真没有它才需要靠轮询感知变化。
optionExplanations_en: Expensive writes are a real limit: every write has to broadcast through the leader and wait on a majority, so high-frequency writes hit the wall first.
The memory-bound storage model caps capacity: a single znode must stay under a megabyte and the whole dataset has to fit in memory — not for bulk data.
Operational complexity is a real pain point: JVM heap tuning, a dedicated log disk, timeout and connection monitoring — simple to use, full of detail to operate.
Watch support is actually its signature strength, not a limitation — it is the absence of watches that would force polling, so this has it backwards.

scenario: 设计 Facebook Live Comments / YouTube Live Chat：百万观众看同一直播，希望同一直播间的 websocket 连接尽量集中到同一台（组）服务器以减少跨服务器通信。
scenario_en: You are designing Facebook Live Comments or YouTube Live Chat. Millions of viewers watch the same stream, and you want connections for one room concentrated on the same server group to reduce cross-server traffic.
q: ZooKeeper 在这里扮演什么角色？
q_en: What role does ZooKeeper play in this live-chat routing design?
options: 让 ZooKeeper 直接充当消息队列，转发全部实时评论的消息本体内容，省去额外组件，架构看起来更简单，还能少维护一套 Kafka
把每一条历史评论的完整内容都存进 ZooKeeper 里，方便日后回放
作为 API 网关的协调点：维护「哪个房间/直播由哪台服务器负责」的映射；服务器带容量注册，新连接按房间查 ZK 定向
给每一条实时评论单独加一把分布式锁，用来防止重复展示
options_en: Have ZooKeeper act as the message queue itself, forwarding all live-comment bodies, dropping extra components so the architecture looks simpler and saves running a separate Kafka.
Store the full content of every historical comment inside ZooKeeper for later replay.
Act as the API gateway's coordination point, mapping which server handles which room, with capacity-aware registration and routing.
Put an individual distributed lock on each live comment to prevent it from being shown twice.
why: 这是「智能路由/同房间同服务器（colocation）」的高级用法——Staff+ 或深度分布式面试的加分项。
why_en: ZooKeeper coordinates smart routing by mapping rooms to servers so a gateway can colocate all viewers of a stream on the same server group.
whenOtherWins: 普通规模的聊天用 pub/sub 广播就能绕开大部分协调问题，不必上这套。
tradeoff: ZK 做房间→服务器的协调映射（轻量、可扩展）vs 把评论本体也塞进 ZK（违反小数据原则、写爆）

termDefinitions.meaning: colocation（同机集中路由）：把同一房间/直播的所有连接尽量路由到同一台或同一组服务器，减少跨服务器通信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Colocation routing means directing all connections for the same room or stream to the same server or server group, minimizing cross-server chatter.

optionExplanations: 让 ZooKeeper 直接转发评论内容会把它当成高吞吐消息队列用，违背了它只放小量协调数据的定位。
把每条历史评论存进 ZooKeeper 同样违反小数据原则，量一大写路径直接被压垮。
对：ZK 作为网关的协调点，维护『哪个房间由哪台服务器负责』的映射，服务器带容量注册，新连接按房间查 ZK 定向。
给每条评论单独加锁是过度设计，评论展示不是需要互斥的临界资源，这解决的是另一个问题。
optionExplanations_en: Making ZooKeeper forward comment bodies treats it as a high-throughput message queue, violating its role of holding only small coordination data.
Storing every historical comment in ZooKeeper also breaks the small-data principle — volume alone would crush the write path.
Right: ZooKeeper is the gateway's coordination point, mapping which server owns which room, with capacity-aware server registration and new connections routed by looking up the room.
Locking each individual comment is over-engineering — displaying a comment is not a critical section needing mutual exclusion; that solves a different problem.

scenario: 自建分布式消息队列：几十个 broker、上千分区，每秒百万条消息本体要落盘。
scenario_en: You are building a distributed message queue with dozens of brokers and thousands of partitions, persisting a million message bodies per second.
q: 设计「分布式消息队列」时，ZooKeeper 可以作为共识大脑承担哪些职责？（多选）
q_en: In a distributed message queue, which responsibilities can ZooKeeper handle as the consensus brain? (Select all that apply.)
options: broker 注册与发现、topic 元数据（分区数、副本因子）存储
每个分区的 leader 选举（顺序临时节点保证单一 leader）
consumer group 成员关系与分区分配，broker 故障经临时节点触发分区重分配
存储全部消息本体，让 broker 直接从 ZK 读写消息内容
options_en: Broker registration and discovery, plus topic metadata like partition count and replication factor.
Per-partition leader election, using sequential ephemeral nodes to guarantee a single leader.
Consumer group membership and partition assignment, with broker failure triggering reassignment via ephemeral nodes.
Storing the full message payloads so brokers read and write message content directly from ZooKeeper.
why: KRaft 之前的 Kafka 正是这么用 ZK 的；HBase、Hadoop、Solr 也是类似模式。消息本体走 broker 自己的日志存储，绝不放 ZK。
why_en: In a distributed queue design ZooKeeper handles broker registration, topic metadata, partition leader election, consumer membership, and failure detection, never the message payloads.
tradeoff: ZK 管协调元数据（小、强一致）vs broker 自管消息日志（大、高吞吐）——两者不能互换

termDefinitions.meaning: broker：消息队列集群里负责接收、存储、转发消息的服务器节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A broker is a server node in a message-queue cluster responsible for receiving, storing, and forwarding messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: consumer group（消费组）：一组共同消费同一批分区、彼此分摊负载的消费者客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer group is a set of consumer clients that jointly consume a set of partitions, sharing the load among themselves.

optionExplanations: broker 注册与 topic 元数据是典型的协调元数据，量小、变化不频繁，正是 ZK 的强项。
分区 leader 选举靠顺序临时节点保证同一时刻只有一个 leader，崩溃后自动换人。
consumer group 成员和分区分配也走同一套机制：broker 故障后临时节点消失，触发重分配。
存储全部消息本体量太大，违反 ZNode 小数据的设计前提，这活儿该交给 broker 自己的日志。
optionExplanations_en: Broker registration and topic metadata is classic small, low-churn coordination data — exactly ZooKeeper's strength.
Partition leader election uses sequential ephemeral nodes to guarantee exactly one leader at a time, with automatic handoff on a crash.
Consumer group membership and partition assignment ride the same mechanism — a broker failure removes its ephemeral node and triggers reassignment.
Storing full message payloads is far too much data, violating the small-znode design premise — that belongs in the broker's own log.

scenario: 分布式文件系统需要「目录及其文件」的嵌套锁获取，要防死锁，还要能监控整个锁层级的变化。
scenario_en: A distributed file system needs nested locks for directories and files. It must avoid deadlocks and watch changes across the whole lock hierarchy.
q: 为什么这里 ZooKeeper 严格优于 Redis？
q_en: Why is ZooKeeper strictly better than Redis in this case?
options: 因为部署 ZooKeeper 集群的机器成本比部署 Redis 更加便宜
ZK 的层级命名空间天然表达父子锁结构，能同时 watch 多个节点监控整个锁层级；Redis 缺少层级与联动通知
因为 Redis 这个产品根本就没有实现过分布式锁的能力
因为 ZooKeeper 锁的整体写入吞吐量比 Redis 锁要高出许多，纯粹的加解锁性能才是这里唯一需要考虑的决定因素
options_en: Because running a ZooKeeper cluster costs less hardware than running Redis.
ZooKeeper's hierarchical namespace naturally expresses parent-child lock structure and can watch multiple nodes across the whole hierarchy; Redis lacks that hierarchy and linked notification.
Because Redis as a product has never implemented any distributed-lock capability.
Because ZooKeeper locks have far higher write throughput than Redis locks, and raw lock/unlock performance is the only factor that matters here.
why: 资源有父子关系、锁获取要尊重层级时，ZK 的树形结构 + 多点 watch 是量身定制；Redis 锁是平面的。
why_en: ZooKeeper's hierarchical namespace and multi-node watches express nested directory-file locks with deadlock prevention, which flat Redis locks cannot.
whenOtherWins: 普通的单资源短锁（订单、座位）Redis 又快又简单，是默认选择。
tradeoff: ZooKeeper 的层级命名空间+多点 watch（表达父子锁结构）vs Redis 的平面 key 空间（无天然层级）
codeSample:
# 目录锁和文件锁按路径天然嵌套
create -e /locks/dir-a lock-owner
create -e /locks/dir-a/file-1 lock-owner

# 同时 watch 父路径和子路径，任一层变化都能感知
zk.exists("/locks/dir-a", true);
zk.exists("/locks/dir-a/file-1", true);
# Redis 的 key 空间是平面的，没有等价的父子层级可 watch

rows: 会话超时自动删除节点

termDefinitions.meaning: 层级命名空间：像文件系统一样用路径组织节点的结构，天然表达父子/嵌套关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hierarchical namespace organizes nodes by path like a filesystem, naturally expressing parent-child nested relationships.

optionExplanations: 机器成本从来不是这道题的决定性约束，问的是『能不能表达父子锁层级』这个能力差异。
对：ZK 的层级命名空间天然表达父子锁结构，能同时 watch 多个节点监控整个锁层级；Redis 是平面 key 空间，没有这种天然层级。
Redis 完全能做分布式锁（SETNX/TTL），说它『没实现过』是事实错误。
吞吐量恰恰是 ZK 锁的弱项而不是优势，这道题赢在能表达父子锁层级，而不是速度。
optionExplanations_en: Hardware cost was never the decisive constraint here — the question is about the ability to express parent-child lock hierarchy.

Right: ZooKeeper's hierarchical namespace naturally expresses parent-child lock structure and can watch multiple nodes to monitor the whole hierarchy; Redis's flat key space has no such native hierarchy.
Redis can absolutely do distributed locks with SETNX and TTL — claiming it never implemented locking is factually wrong.
Throughput is actually a weakness of ZK locks, not a strength; this case is won by expressing parent-child lock hierarchy, not by speed.

scenario: 普通产品向系统设计面试（非深度基础设施），你在考虑要不要把 ZooKeeper 画进架构图。
scenario_en: In a regular product-oriented system design interview, not a deep infrastructure interview, you are deciding whether to draw ZooKeeper into the architecture.
q: 正确的姿态是？
q_en: What is the right posture toward ZooKeeper in this interview setting?
options: 不管拿到什么题目，一上来就先在架构图里画一个 ZooKeeper 集群，显得自己考虑得很周全、很有分布式经验
干脆用 ZooKeeper 去替代设计里原本该用的所有数据库
别急着上 ZK：除非在设计深度基础设施系统、需要精细协调，或需求超出现代负载均衡器/内置服务发现的能力
不管遇到什么场景，面试全程都绝口不提 ZooKeeper 这个词
options_en: Whatever the prompt, immediately draw a ZooKeeper cluster into the architecture to look thorough and experienced with distributed systems.
Just go ahead and replace every database in the design with ZooKeeper instead.
Do not reach for ZooKeeper unless designing deep infrastructure, needing fine-grained coordination, or the need exceeds modern load balancers and built-in discovery.
No matter what scenario comes up, never mention the word ZooKeeper at all during the interview.
why: ZK 很少是第一选择：现代 LB、平台服务发现、云托管方案覆盖了多数场景；它的主场是深度 infra 题和高级协调需求。
why_en: Do not reach for ZooKeeper unless you are designing deep infrastructure or need coordination beyond what modern load balancers and built-in service discovery offer.
whenOtherWins: 设计分布式消息队列/任务调度器、或需要智能路由与层级锁时，ZK 就是合理选择。
tradeoff: ZK 的精细协调能力（重、需要额外运维）vs 现代 LB/托管服务发现（轻量、覆盖大多数产品场景）
optionExplanations: 不管题目是什么都先画 ZooKeeper，会让面试官觉得你缺乏『先问需求再选组件』的判断力。
把 ZooKeeper 当数据库替代品混淆了协调服务和数据存储两种不同定位，它扛不住高吞吐读写。
对：除非在设计深度基础设施、需要精细协调，或需求超出现代负载均衡器/内置服务发现的能力，否则别急着上 ZK。
完全不提这个知识点是矫枉过正，真遇到需要它的深度 infra 题时反而说不出方案。
optionExplanations_en: Drawing ZooKeeper for every prompt signals to the interviewer that you lack the judgment to clarify requirements before picking components.
Treating ZooKeeper as a database replacement conflates a coordination service with data storage — it cannot handle high-throughput reads and writes.
Right: do not reach for ZooKeeper unless you are designing deep infrastructure, need fine-grained coordination, or the need exceeds what modern load balancers and built-in service discovery cover.
Never mentioning it at all is overcorrecting — you would have nothing to say when a genuinely deep infra question calls for it.

scenario: 聊天服务器向 5 节点 ensemble 写入 Bob 的新路由，写确认之后绝不允许回退。
scenario_en: A chat server writes Bob's new routing to a five-node ensemble, and once the write is acknowledged it must never roll back.
q: 一次写请求（如注册 Bob 的 ZNode）在 ensemble 内部的流转是？
q_en: How does a write request, such as registering Bob's ZNode, flow through the ensemble?
options: 任意一台 follower 收到写请求后直接写本地磁盘，就可以立刻返回写成功
请求到 leader → leader 向所有 follower 广播变更 → 多数派确认已接受并保存 → leader 确认写成功
客户端把同一条写请求原样同时发送给 ensemble 里的每一台服务器
每台服务器先各自把数据写到本地磁盘，之后再统一去问 leader 这次写到底有没有效，顺序整个反过来，省掉一次等待，效率反而更高
options_en: Any follower that receives the write just writes to its local disk and returns success right away.
The request reaches the leader, which broadcasts the change to followers, and it succeeds once a majority has accepted and saved it.
The client sends the exact same write request to every single server in the ensemble at once.
Each server first writes the data to its own local disk, then afterward asks the leader whether the write was valid — the order reversed, saving a round of waiting and supposedly faster.
why: 写必须过 leader 并拿到 quorum 确认——这正是写比读贵、但一致性有保障的原因。
why_en: A write goes to the leader, which broadcasts it to followers and confirms success once a majority has accepted and saved it.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["Client write"] --> B["Leader proposal"]
  B --> C["Quorum ack"]
  C --> D["Commit"]
  D --> E["Watch events"]
optionExplanations: follower 收到写请求不能自己直接确认成功，那样多个 follower 各自确认会破坏全序保证。
对：请求先到 leader，leader 向所有 follower 广播变更，多数派确认已接受并保存后 leader 才确认写成功。
客户端不会把同一条写请求原样同时发给每台服务器，写入必须先经过 leader 统一排序。
每台服务器各自先写本地磁盘再问 leader，顺序反了——必须先经 leader 排序广播，服务器才落盘。
optionExplanations_en: A follower cannot just confirm a write itself — if several followers each confirmed independently, the total-order guarantee would break.
Right: the request goes to the leader first, which broadcasts the change to all followers, and only confirms success once a majority has accepted and saved it.
The client does not fire the same write to every server at once — writes must first be ordered through the leader.
Servers writing to local disk first and asking the leader after has the order backwards — the leader must sequence and broadcast before servers persist.

scenario: 团队在讨论要不要把一份几 MB 的完整用户资料 JSON 直接存进一个 ZNode，还是只存一个指向对象存储的引用。
scenario_en: The team is deciding whether to store a multi-MB user profile JSON directly in one ZNode or store only a pointer to object storage.
q: ZooKeeper 默认配置下，单个 ZNode 的数据大小硬上限大约是多少？
q_en: Under ZooKeeper's default configuration, roughly what is the hard size limit for a single znode's data?
options: 1KB：超过就会被拒绝
10MB：几 MB 的 JSON 可以直接放
约 1MB（默认 jute.maxbuffer）；实际应远小于此，典型在字节到 KB 级
1GB：ZNode 可以当文件存储用
options_en: 1 KB: anything larger is rejected
10 MB: a multi-MB JSON fits directly
About 1 MB (default jute.maxbuffer); in practice keep it far smaller, typically bytes to kilobytes
1 GB: a znode can serve as file storage
why: 默认 jute.maxbuffer 约 1MB，单 znode 超过会被拒绝；但官方明确 ZooKeeper 不是通用数据库或大对象存储，znode 数据通常是字节到 KB 级，且整个数据集要装进内存。几 MB 的 JSON 应放对象存储/DB，ZNode 只存引用。
why_en: The default jute.maxbuffer is about 1 MB, and larger znode data is rejected; but the docs are clear that ZooKeeper is not a general database or large-object store — znode data is usually bytes to kilobytes, and the whole dataset must fit in memory. A multi-MB JSON belongs in object storage or a DB, with only a reference in the znode.

scenario: 配置聊天服务器的 ZooKeeper 客户端会话超时参数，要在「网络抖动误判」和「故障发现太慢」之间找平衡。
scenario_en: You are configuring the ZooKeeper client session timeout for chat servers and need to balance false failure detection from network jitter against slow real-failure detection.
q: ZooKeeper 会话超时的典型配置区间是？
q_en: What is the typical ZooKeeper session timeout range?
options: 10-30 毫秒，几乎任何一次网络抖动都会触发误判
10-30 秒，兼顾故障发现速度和抗网络抖动能力
10-30 分钟，故障发现会慢到影响用户体验
10-30 小时，几乎等于关闭了故障检测能力
options_en: 10-30 milliseconds, where almost any network blip triggers a false failure.
10-30 seconds, balancing fast failure detection against tolerance for network blips.
10-30 minutes, slow enough to noticeably hurt user experience during a real failure.
10-30 hours, which effectively disables failure detection.
why: 10-30 秒是「误报 vs 检测速度」的常见折中——短于此网络抖动就会引发误判切换，长于此真故障要等太久才被发现，而这个窗口也正是临时节点消失、下游 watcher 收到通知的时间量级。
why_en: Session timeouts are typically ten to thirty seconds, balancing false-positive failovers against how long real failure detection via ephemeral nodes takes.

q: 补全 ZooKeeper 的三大基础原语：
q_en: Fill in ZooKeeper's three basic primitives.
text: ZooKeeper 靠三个简单原语组合出所有协调能力：{{ZNode}}（层级命名空间中的数据节点）、可靠的服务器 {{ensemble}}（多数派容错）、{{watch}}（变更实时通知）。
why: 数据模型 + 可靠集群 + 通知机制——三件套组合出配置管理、服务发现、选举与锁的全部配方。
why_en: ZooKeeper combines znodes in a hierarchical namespace, a reliable server ensemble, and watches for change notification.

termDefinitions.meaning: ZNode：层级命名空间里的一个数据节点，能存少量数据、能有子节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A znode is a node in the hierarchical namespace that can hold a small amount of data and have children.

termDefinitions.meaning: ensemble：一组协同工作、以多数派（quorum）容错的 ZooKeeper 服务器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ensemble is the group of ZooKeeper servers working together with majority-based fault tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: watch：客户端登记在 ZNode 上的一次性变更通知。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A watch is a one-time change notification a client registers on a znode.

scenario: 两台聊天服务器几乎同时对同一个 /users/bob 节点调 setData，各写自己算出的新位置。
scenario_en: Two chat servers call setData on the same /users/bob znode at almost the same moment, each writing its own computed location.
q: 调 setData 时把 version 参数传 -1，并发下会怎样？
q_en: What happens under concurrency if you pass version = -1 to setData?
options: 传 -1 表示用当前版本号做 CAS，版本不符就拒绝，天然挡住并发覆盖
传 -1 表示忽略版本、无条件覆盖，后写直接盖掉先写，成丢失更新
传 -1 会让 ZooKeeper 自动合并两次写的差异，两边更新都保留下来
传 -1 会阻塞第二个写，直到第一个提交完成，把两次更新串行化
options_en: -1 means do a CAS against the current version and reject on mismatch, blocking concurrent overwrites.
-1 means ignore the version and overwrite unconditionally, so the later write clobbers the earlier one.
-1 makes ZooKeeper auto-merge the two writes so both updates are kept.
-1 blocks the second write until the first commits, serializing the two updates.
why: -1 忽略版本做无条件覆盖，并发下后写覆盖先写=丢失更新；要安全就把读到的版本号传进去做 CAS，代价是版本不符要重读重试。
why_en: Passing -1 overwrites unconditionally so concurrent writers lose updates; pass the version you read to make it a CAS that costs a re-read on conflict.
codeSample:
# 无条件覆盖：忽略版本，后写必赢（可能丢更新）
zk.setData("/chat-app/users/bob", "server3", -1)
# CAS 写：仅当节点版本仍是 7 才成功，否则抛 BadVersion 需重读
zk.setData("/chat-app/users/bob", "server3", 7)
optionExplanations: 记反了：-1 恰恰是「忽略版本」；真正的 CAS 要传你读到的那个版本号，不是 -1。
对：-1 让写无条件生效，两台并发写时后到的直接覆盖先到的，先写的改动就丢了。
ZooKeeper 不做值合并，只按顺序覆盖；「自动合并」是把它当成了 CRDT 那类系统。
setData 不替你排队阻塞并发写，谁后到谁生效，没有自动串行化这回事。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: -1 means ignore the version; a real CAS passes the version you read, not -1.
Right: -1 applies the write unconditionally, so the later concurrent write overwrites the earlier one and its change is lost.
ZooKeeper never merges values, it only overwrites in order; auto-merge treats it like a CRDT-style system.
setData does not queue or block concurrent writes; the later one simply wins, with no auto-serialization.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAS(比较并交换)：只有当数据的版本/值仍等于你读到的那个时写才成功，否则失败，用来做无锁并发控制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Compare-And-Swap succeeds only if the value or version still equals the one you read, otherwise it fails — a lock-free way to guard concurrent writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 版本号(version)：每个 ZNode 每被修改一次就自增的计数器，setData 可带上它做条件写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Each ZNode has a version counter that increments on every change; setData can pass it to make the write conditional.

termDefinitions.meaning: 丢失更新：两个写并发发生，后提交的直接覆盖先提交的，先写的改动无声消失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lost update is when two concurrent writes race and the later one overwrites the earlier, silently discarding the first change.

termDefinitions.meaning: CRDT(无冲突复制数据类型)：能自动合并并发修改而不丢数据的数据结构，ZK 并不是这类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Conflict-free Replicated Data Type auto-merges concurrent edits without losing data; ZooKeeper is not one of these.

scenario: 你想让「唯一一台」服务器负责跑支付处理和定时任务，其余待命，它崩了要自动有人接班。
scenario_en: You want exactly one server to run payment processing and scheduled jobs, with the rest on standby and automatic takeover if it dies.
q: 该用应用级 leader 选举，还是每次操作抢分布式锁？
q_en: Should you use application-level leader election or grab a distributed lock per operation?
options: 用分布式锁：每台服务器每次跑支付前抢一次锁，用完立刻释放
用 leader 选举：选一台长期持有该角色，崩了下一台自动接班
两者其实完全等价，反正都靠顺序临时节点实现，随便挑一个用就行了
都不用，让每台服务器都跑支付，靠数据库唯一约束事后去重
options_en: Use a distributed lock: each server grabs the lock before every payment run and releases it right after.
Use leader election: one server holds the role long-term and the next takes over automatically if it dies.
They are equivalent — both use sequential ephemeral nodes, so just pick either one.
Skip both: let every server run payments and de-duplicate afterward with a database unique constraint.
why: 支付/调度要的是「长期只有一台在跑这个角色」，leader 选举给你持续独占+自动故障转移；分布式锁只保证单次操作互斥、用完就放，撑不起长期独占。
why_en: Payments and scheduling need one server to own the role long-term, which leader election gives with auto-failover; a lock only enforces per-operation mutual exclusion.
whenOtherWins: 当你只需要在一小段临界区里互斥（如卖票时扣一次库存），用完立即释放，分布式锁更合适。
tradeoff: leader 选举「长期角色归属+自动接班」 vs 分布式锁「单次操作互斥+即用即放」
optionExplanations: 锁是围绕单次操作的互斥，支付角色要长期独占，锁一放开别的服务器就能抢进来，守不住。
对：选举让一台长期担这个角色，它崩了下一台顺序接班，正好匹配「持续只有一台在跑」。
两者都用顺序临时节点当积木，但语义不同：一个管长期角色，一个管单次互斥，不能混用。
让所有机器都跑再事后去重，等于放弃了「同一时刻只有一台在处理」，重复副作用已经发生。
optionExplanations_en: A lock guards a single operation; once released another server can grab it, so it cannot hold a long-term role.
Right: election makes one server own the role long-term and the next takes over on crash — exactly "one at a time".
Both use sequential ephemeral nodes as blocks, but the semantics differ: long-term role vs single-shot exclusion.
Running everywhere and de-duping later abandons "only one at a time" — the duplicate side effects already happened.

termDefinitions.meaning: leader 选举：在一组对等服务器中选出唯一一台长期承担某职责，它失效时自动换下一台。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Leader election picks one server from a peer group to own a role long-term, automatically promoting the next if it fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式锁：跨机器的互斥原语，同一时刻只有一个客户端持有，用来保护共享资源避免竞态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock is a cross-machine mutual-exclusion primitive held by one client at a time to guard a shared resource.

termDefinitions.meaning: 顺序临时节点：名字带自增序号、且会话结束即消失的 ZNode，是 ZK 选举和锁共用的积木。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequential ephemeral znode has an auto-incrementing suffix and vanishes when the session ends — the shared building block for ZK election and locks.

scenario: ZooKeeper 集群里一台 follower 因网络抖动短暂掉线，期间 leader 又提交了好几批写。
scenario_en: A follower in a ZooKeeper ensemble briefly drops off due to a network blip, and the leader commits several batches of writes while it is gone.
q: 这台 follower 重连后，如何恢复到和其他节点一致的视图？
q_en: After reconnecting, how does this follower get back to a view consistent with the others?
options: 直接继续服务读，漏掉的写等下次客户端写它时顺带补齐
跟 leader 跑追赶同步，重放漏掉的事务，追平后才对外服务读
清空自己全部数据，当作全新节点从头全量拉一遍快照
掉线期间它其实一条写都没漏，因为 follower 也全程参与了每次提交
options_en: Keep serving reads immediately; the missed writes get patched in the next time a client writes to it.
Run catch-up synchronization with the leader, replay the missed transactions, then serve reads once caught up.
Wipe all its data and pull a full snapshot from scratch as if it were a brand-new node.
It actually missed no writes at all, because a follower takes part in every commit even while disconnected.
why: 正常时 follower 内存副本紧跟 leader；掉线就落后成陈旧副本；重连后靠同步协议追赶、重放漏掉的事务才恢复 single system image；代价：追平前从它读可能读到旧值。
why_en: A lagging follower catches up by replaying the writes it missed before it can serve consistent reads; until it catches up, reads from it can be stale.
optionExplanations: 继续服务读=对外吐陈旧数据，且写只落在被写的那个节点，靠它捎带补不齐整段漏掉的历史。
对：落后的 follower 先跟 leader 追平漏掉的事务，追上后才恢复一致视图再对外读。
全量拉快照只在落后太多时才需要；一般小差距重放事务日志即可，清空重来是过度动作。
follower 掉线就收不到 leader 的提交广播，确实会漏写，「全程参与」与掉线自相矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: Serving reads means emitting stale data, and a write only lands on the node written — it cannot backfill missed history.
Right: the lagging follower first replays the transactions it missed, then serves a consistent view again.
A full snapshot is only needed when a follower is too far behind; a small gap just replays the log — wiping is overkill.
A disconnected follower stops receiving the commit broadcast, so it does miss writes; "took part in every commit" contradicts being offline.

termDefinitions.meaning: follower(跟随者)：ZK 集群里非 leader 的服务器，复制 leader 的状态并直接服务读请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A follower is a non-leader server in the ensemble that replicates the leader's state and serves read requests directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单一系统映像：不管连到哪台服务器，客户端(同步后)看到的都是同一份系统视图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Single system image means a client sees the same view of the system regardless of which server it connects to, once synchronized.

termDefinitions.meaning: 追赶同步：落后的 follower 重连后向 leader 补拉并重放掉线期间漏掉的事务，直到追平。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Catch-up synchronization is when a lagging follower replays the transactions it missed from the leader until it is up to date.

termDefinitions.meaning: 快照(snapshot)：ZK 内存数据库的周期性磁盘镜像，重启时先加载它再重放日志加速恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A snapshot is a periodic on-disk image of ZooKeeper's in-memory database, loaded first on restart to speed recovery before replaying logs.

scenario: ZooKeeper 每次写都要先把事务 fsync 落盘才返回成功，而它内部所有操作是全序处理的。
scenario_en: ZooKeeper fsyncs every transaction to disk before returning success, and it processes all operations in a single total order.
q: 把事务日志和快照、其它 IO 挤在同一块磁盘上，会有什么后果？
q_en: What happens if you put the transaction log on the same disk as snapshots and other I/O?
options: 没影响，数据反正最终都落到同一块盘，顺序写快慢都一样
fsync 要和别的 IO 抢盘，写延迟一抖，全序队列后面全被拖慢
只有生成快照那一刻会慢，平时的读写完全不受磁盘争用影响
无所谓，ZooKeeper 会把事务日志全缓存在内存里，根本不落磁盘
options_en: No impact — the data all lands on the same disk anyway, so sequential writes are just as fast.
fsync now contends for the disk; one latency spike stalls every request queued behind it in the total order.
Only the moment a snapshot is written is slow; normal reads and writes are unaffected by disk contention.
It does not matter — ZooKeeper keeps the whole transaction log in memory and never hits the disk.
why: 事务日志是 ZK 最性能攸关的部分：必须先 fsync 再返回，又因操作全序，一次慢盘写会把整条队列拖垮，所以官方建议配独立日志盘；代价是多一块专用磁盘设备。
why_en: The transaction log must fsync before acking, and since ops are totally ordered, one slow write stalls the whole queue — so give it a dedicated disk.
optionExplanations: 同一块盘上 fsync 要和快照写、系统 IO 争用磁头/带宽，写延迟并不「一样」，会被拖高。
对：先 fsync 才返回，再叠加全序，一次慢盘写就把排在后面的所有请求一起卡住。
不止快照那一刻：任何与日志抢盘的 IO 都会抬高 fsync 延迟，进而影响平时每次写。
事务日志必须先 fsync 真正落盘才返回，把它「全缓存在内存不落盘」直接违背持久化前提。
optionExplanations_en: On one disk, fsync competes with snapshot writes and system I/O for the head and bandwidth, so latency is not "the same".
Right: fsync-before-ack plus total ordering means one slow disk write jams every request queued behind it.
Not just at snapshot time: any I/O competing with the log raises fsync latency and thus every normal write.
The transaction log must fsync to disk before acking; keeping it wholly in memory breaks the durability premise.

termDefinitions.meaning: fsync：强制把文件改动从操作系统缓存刷到物理磁盘的系统调用，返回后数据才算真正持久化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: fsync is a system call that forces buffered file changes out to physical disk, so data is truly durable only after it returns.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事务日志：ZK 把每个状态变更先顺序写入的预写日志(WAL)，保证已确认的更新崩溃也不丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The transaction log is a write-ahead log where ZooKeeper records every state change first, so acknowledged updates survive a crash.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全序：所有写请求被排成唯一一条线性顺序依次处理，因此队头一慢，后面全部跟着等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Total order means all writes are processed in one single linear sequence, so a slow item at the head makes everything behind it wait.

termDefinitions.meaning: 快照(snapshot)：ZK 内存数据库的周期性磁盘镜像，重启时先加载它再重放日志加速恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A snapshot is a periodic on-disk image of ZooKeeper's in-memory database, loaded first on restart to speed recovery before replaying logs.
